paragraphs.procedure: Share the management philosophy as a direction for decisions and standards as work criteria; use budgeting to define targets and control items for each period. Use specific performance-appraisal facts and training needs to improve operations. Appoint trainers and trainees, create a training program combining OJT and OffJT, and include training time in work schedules.
paragraphs.mistakes: The textbook gives reference examples such as sales per labor-hour of 5,000 yen, gross profit per labor-hour of 4,000 yen, monthly labor productivity of 700,000 yen, and a labor distribution ratio of 35–40%. These are not statutory wages or pass marks for every restaurant. Conditions differ by business format, spending per customer, cost structure, and period. State the basis and comparison period for targets, and do not sacrifice safety or service for profit alone.
paragraphs.scenario: After a week below budget, the supervisor first compares plan and actual performance. They separate spending per customer, customer count, costs, staffing, and training shortfalls, then implement the necessary improvements. The following week, they evaluate using consistently defined indicators and workplace observation, feeding revisions into the next plan. Do not alter records merely to make figures look better.

rst-2-ops-17.summary: Align definitions and comparison conditions, connecting planning, training, action, evaluation, and revision in restaurant management.
rst-2-ops-17.activity: Classify 20 terms for 8 minutes; check ratio denominators in a 7-minute exercise; plan training and staffing for 8 minutes; explain why reference targets must be adapted to the restaurant’s plan for 7 minutes.

rst-1-week01-q01.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-1-week01-q01.stem: A staple has come loose near a dish. Which hazard should you consider?
rst-1-week01-q01.explanation: Metal fragments are a physical hazard that can cause injury if they enter food. Check nearby food and locate the staple, then report it.

rst-1-week01-q02.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-1-week01-q02.stem: What is the problem with using raw-meat tongs to plate cooked meat too?
options: They may transfer bacteria to cooked food
The meat’s weight will always increase
The plating temperature will always drop
rst-1-week01-q02.explanation: Even if heating reduces bacteria, raw-meat utensils can contaminate the food again. Use separate utensils for each purpose.

rst-1-week01-q03.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-1-week01-q03.stem: What is the main purpose of taking cold ingredients out in small batches while working?
options: To leave them at room temperature for longer
To make packaging easier to tear
To shorten the time outside cold temperature control
rst-1-week01-q03.explanation: Taking out only what is needed reduces time left at room temperature. The purpose is not to extend the date.

rst-1-week01-q04.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-1-week01-q04.stem: Which is appropriate when handling raw chicken to control Campylobacter?
options: Serve it raw without conditions if fresh
Heat thoroughly and prevent contamination of other food
Make heating unnecessary by marinating in seasonings
Serve after only cooling the surface
rst-1-week01-q04.explanation: Campylobacter is a concern in chicken and similar foods. Freshness or seasoning alone cannot guarantee safety.

rst-1-week01-q05.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-1-week01-q05.stem: What should you be aware of when soil attached to rice, beans, or similar ingredients is brought into the kitchen?
options: Food contamination by microorganisms found in nature
The presence of soil makes disinfection unnecessary
Soil can be mixed directly into food if dry
rst-1-week01-q05.explanation: Soil can contain microorganisms such as Bacillus cereus. Hygienic control of ingredients and work areas is necessary.

rst-1-week01-q06.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-1-week01-q06.stem: A storage problem is found when receiving red-fleshed fish. Why must you not assume cooking alone solves it?
options: Fish always becomes poisonous when heated
Some hazards, such as histamine, are not resolved by heating
Soy sauce can always remove the hazard
rst-1-week01-q06.explanation: Effective measures vary by hazard. Do not accept a hazard from improper storage simply because cooking is planned.

rst-1-week01-q07.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-1-week01-q07.stem: The product name and quantity match the delivery note. What check is needed next?
options: Finish receiving inspection without opening anything if the quantity matches
Quality, including packaging, dates and storage conditions
Recheck only the prices on the delivery note
Skip checking the temperature if the delivery address is correct
rst-1-week01-q07.explanation: Receiving inspection requires checking the actual product’s quality and storage conditions as well as matching the paperwork.

rst-1-week01-q08.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-1-week01-q08.stem: An ingredient arrives with an unreadable date label. What is the appropriate action?
options: Copy the date from the same product
Write the receiving date as the expiry date
Remove the packaging and discard the date label
Confirm with the person in charge or supplier before deciding acceptance
rst-1-week01-q08.explanation: Do not leave an unconfirmed date unresolved or label it by guesswork. Obtain accurate information.

rst-2-week01-q01.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-2-week01-q01.stem: A hygiene plan was stamped “checked” before the work began. What corrective action should the person in charge take?
options: Make advance stamping the official method
Treat additional stamps as proof of safety
Teach checking and recording at the time of the actual work and verify what happens
Remove the forms and rely only on verbal promises
rst-2-week01-q01.explanation: Records must be based on actual checks. Stamping in advance makes it impossible to establish whether control was carried out.

rst-2-week01-q02.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-2-week01-q02.stem: More cleaning tools were added, but they are not separated by area and are shared with contaminated areas. What is the improvement?
options: Separate purposes and storage locations and train staff to use the tools accordingly
Use the same tools in a different order
Increase only the number of tools again
Do not separate them until dirt becomes visible
rst-2-week01-q02.explanation: Clarify purposes, storage, and treatment after use, not just the number of tools, to prevent contamination across areas.

rst-2-week01-q03.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-2-week01-q03.stem: A worker wants to replace a grease-cleaning product with an acidic cleaner without authorization. What is the appropriate judgment?
options: Assume all cleaners have the same effect
Choose the one with a strong smell
Mix chemicals to increase the effect
Choose after checking the dirt, material, and product’s intended use
rst-2-week01-q03.explanation: Use cleaners according to the nature of the dirt, utensil material, and product label. Mixing on your own judgment is dangerous.

rst-2-week01-q04.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-2-week01-q04.stem: Detergent and disinfectant are being transferred into beverage bottles. What should the person in charge do?
options: Allow it if staff remember the colors
Correct this by using labelled, dedicated containers that prevent accidental drinking and misuse
Put them in the food refrigerator to distinguish them
Remove labels to make their appearance uniform
rst-2-week01-q04.explanation: Manage chemicals with containers, labels, and storage locations that prevent confusion with food. Do not rely on verbal memory alone.

rst-2-week01-q05.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-2-week01-q05.stem: Disinfected utensils are being returned to a shelf with dirty hands. Which improvement takes priority?
options: Review hygienic handling and storage after disinfection
Unconditionally increase only the chemical concentration
Only add more records of disinfection time
rst-2-week01-q05.explanation: Cleanliness cannot be maintained if recontamination occurs after disinfection. Manage removal, hands, and storage locations together.

rst-2-week01-q06.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-2-week01-q06.stem: Items placed in the handwashing area have made it unusable. What is appropriate facility management?
options: Allow staff to wipe hands at another counter
Skip handwashing until the items are removed
Restore immediate usability and include it in daily checks
rst-2-week01-q06.explanation: Handwashing facilities must be usable when needed. Include obstructions and missing supplies in inspections too.

rst-2-week01-q07.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-2-week01-q07.stem: A worker returned a thermometer that failed calibration to its original place. What prevents reuse?
options: Have just one person remember it is faulty
Identify it as unusable, isolate it, and manage a replacement
Replace the display with a normal reading
Change only its storage location every day
rst-2-week01-q07.explanation: Identification and isolation are needed to keep failed instruments out of use, together with a reliable replacement.

rst-2-week01-q08.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-2-week01-q08.stem: A report says the water has an unusual color. What should the person in charge decide first?
options: Keep using it for cooking if the color is faint
Do not record it until the abnormality disappears
Stop using it and investigate the cause and affected scope
rst-2-week01-q08.explanation: Abnormal water affects food and washing too. Do not hide its appearance; suspend use until safety is confirmed.

rst-1-q001.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q001.stem: Which cooking method is suitable for tenderizing beef shin with a lot of connective tissue?
options: Simmer it slowly for a long time
Only rinse it in cold water
Coat it lightly and serve it raw
rst-1-q001.explanation: Beef shin has a lot of connective tissue, which softens during prolonged simmering. Briefly heating only the surface leaves it tough.

rst-1-q002.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q002.stem: Which knife should you choose to slice sashimi in a drawing cut?
rst-1-q002.explanation: A sashimi knife has a shape suited to slicing sashimi. Use the right tool for the job hygienically.

rst-1-q003.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q003.stem: Your hands are still wet after washing. What should you do next?
options: Wipe them on the hem of your uniform
Dry them using a clean method
Wipe them with a dirty shared cloth
rst-1-q003.explanation: Use a clean drying method that does not recontaminate washed hands. Uniforms and dirty cloths are unsuitable.

rst-1-q004.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q004.stem: What is the main purpose of using separate knives for raw fish and vegetables eaten raw?
options: Make vegetables no longer need cooking
rst-1-q004.explanation: Separating tools by use separates contamination routes. Washing and disinfection are still necessary after separation.

rst-1-q005.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q005.stem: While carrying food, you meet a customer face-to-face in the aisle. What should you do?
rst-1-q005.explanation: Prevent collisions and give priority to the customer’s passage. Take particular care when carrying a tray or hot food.

rst-1-q006.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q006.stem: After cutting raw chicken, you will plate a salad. What should you do first?
options: Only wipe your hands with a cloth
rst-1-q006.explanation: Bacteria from raw meat can transfer through hands. Wearing gloves alone does not replace handwashing.

rst-1-q007.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q007.stem: Which method heats food briefly over high heat with a small amount of oil while moving it?
rst-1-q007.explanation: Stir-frying uses a small amount of oil, high heat, and movement of the food. Steaming uses steam.

rst-1-q008.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q008.stem: Immediately after cleaning the toilet, you are asked to plate food. What should you do first?
options: Rinse only the outside of your gloves
Shake your hands without changing work clothes
Remove cleaning gear and wash your hands thoroughly
Move while still holding the cleaning brush
rst-1-q008.explanation: Keep cleaning equipment separate to avoid bringing contamination into food areas, and wash your hands thoroughly when finished.

rst-1-q009.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q009.stem: In a basic Japanese meal setting, where is the rice placed?
options: At the back right from the diner’s viewpoint
On top of the soup bowl
On the floor outside the chopsticks
rst-1-q009.explanation: The basic arrangement places rice on the left and soup on the right. Also check the actual dishes and the restaurant’s service standards.

rst-1-q010.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q010.stem: Only the outside of a hamburger steak has browned. What is necessary before serving?
options: Accept it based on surface color alone
Warm the plate to make up for undercooking
Check that the center is cooked according to the restaurant’s standard
Hide the red part with sauce
rst-1-q010.explanation: A browned surface does not guarantee cooking at the center. Check using the specified method, such as core temperature.

rst-1-q011.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q011.stem: Which expression accepts a customer’s request?
options: 「お先に失礼します」 — Excuse me for leaving first
「かしこまりました」 — Certainly, I understand
「ただいま留守です」 — We are currently out
rst-1-q011.explanation: When acknowledging and accepting a request, use an expression such as “kashikomarimashita” and follow through with the action.

rst-1-q012.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q012.stem: You do not know whether a customer using a wheelchair needs assistance. What should you do first?
options: Ask the customer what help they would like
Keep speaking only to their companion
Refuse all wheelchair users at the entrance
rst-1-q012.explanation: Support needs vary by person. Confirm the customer’s wishes instead of helping based on assumptions.

rst-1-q013.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q013.stem: What is the problem with leaving cooked food at room temperature for a long time?
options: Room temperature always makes it germ-free
It spends a long time in temperatures where bacteria grow readily
rst-1-q013.explanation: Temperature and time still require control after cooking. A lid or checking smell alone cannot prevent bacterial growth.

rst-1-q014.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q014.stem: Which category includes carrots, lotus roots, and daikon radishes?
rst-1-q014.explanation: Understanding ingredient categories helps organize preparation and storage. The textbook classifies these vegetables as root vegetables.

rst-1-q015.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q015.stem: Which tool measures the core temperature of cooked food?
rst-1-q015.explanation: Use equipment suited to measuring the food’s center, rather than surface or room temperature.

rst-1-q016.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q016.stem: A kitchen fire has spread to the ceiling. What takes priority?
options: Approach and keep fighting it alone
rst-1-q016.explanation: If the fire is intense and dangerous, stop firefighting and prioritize evacuation. Do not continue treating it like a small fire.

rst-1-q017.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q017.stem: A group reservation is expected before opening. What should you check?
options: Share guest numbers, menu details, and seating preparations
Tell the kitchen only after the group arrives
Keep the reservation details only in your own memory
Check only the number of chairs
rst-1-q017.explanation: Reservation information affects both cooking and customer service, so the relevant staff must confirm details and preparations together.

rst-1-q018.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q018.stem: What hygiene step is needed before inserting a thermometer into the center of food?
options: Leave residue from the previous dish
Hold it with a cloth and skip the measurement
rst-1-q018.explanation: Measuring equipment can also transfer contamination. Clean the food-contact part before checking cooking at the center.

rst-1-q019.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q019.stem: Which nutrient–food combination relates to building the body?
rst-1-q019.explanation: Protein in foods such as fish helps build the body. A balanced diet that does not rely on one nutrient alone is also important.

rst-1-q020.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q020.stem: Several customers say the restaurant is too hot. What should you check?
options: Only the color of order slips
rst-1-q020.explanation: Comfort involves temperature, sound, lighting, and other factors. Check the environmental factor raised by the customers.

rst-1-q021.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q021.explanation: Match equipment names to their uses. A rice warmer keeps cooked rice warm.

rst-1-q022.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q022.stem: A waste bin is about to overflow. What is appropriate?
options: Remove the waste promptly using the designated procedure
Push it down with your foot and leave it overnight
Empty it under a preparation table
Transfer it to a food container for storage
rst-1-q022.explanation: Accumulated waste invites contamination and pests. Keep it separate from food and follow the restaurant’s sorting and removal procedures.

rst-1-q023.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q023.stem: The food tastes good, but portions vary each time. What mainly needs improvement?
options: A different order for accepting reservations
rst-1-q023.explanation: Quality includes consistent portions and plating as well as taste. Music or paperwork cannot solve a portion-size problem.

rst-1-q024.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q024.stem: What are the three parts produced when filleting a fish using sanmai-oroshi?
options: Left fillet, right fillet, and backbone
rst-1-q024.explanation: Sanmai-oroshi separates the flesh on both sides along the backbone.

rst-1-q025.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q025.stem: Meat residue remains on a cutting board. What should you do before disinfecting?
options: Only pour disinfectant over the residue
Hide it with a dry cloth
Put clean food on it to check
Wash with detergent to remove residue, then rinse
rst-1-q025.explanation: Disinfection may not work adequately when dirt remains. Wash and rinse first.

rst-1-q026.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q026.stem: A load is too heavy for one person to carry steadily. What is appropriate?
options: Split the load or carry it with two people
Lift it sharply using only your lower back
Carry it without being able to see ahead
Force yourself to carry it all in one trip
rst-1-q026.explanation: Stability and visibility matter as well as weight. Splitting the load or using several people reduces strain.

rst-1-q027.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q027.stem: At the start of work, the refrigerator temperature exceeds the restaurant’s limit. What is appropriate?
options: Rewrite only the displayed value as compliant
Close the door and do not record it
Hide cold food at the back
Check food condition, report, and record the problem
rst-1-q027.explanation: An abnormal refrigerator temperature requires checking the effect on food and taking the prescribed action. Do not alter records.

rst-1-q028.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q028.stem: What is an appropriate way to handle a broken glass?
options: Squeeze the pieces together with bare hands
Put the broken glass in the dishwasher
Collect safely under the restaurant’s procedure and discard separately
rst-1-q028.explanation: Fragments can cause cuts or contaminate food. Protect hands and control where fragments are and how they are discarded.

rst-1-q029.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q029.stem: You are returning to work immediately after blowing your nose. What is appropriate?
options: Skip handwashing once the tissue is discarded
Wash your hands hygienically before returning
Use only the hand that looks cleaner
rst-1-q029.explanation: Hands that touched the nose or a used tissue can transfer contamination, so handwashing is necessary.

rst-1-q030.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q030.stem: You are unsure whether a cashless payment completed. What should you do?
options: Check the terminal result and restaurant procedure
Write the customer’s card number in a personal note
rst-1-q030.explanation: Confirm payment status to prevent double charging or nonpayment. Do not privately record payment information.

rst-1-q031.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q031.stem: What is appropriate when preparing a cleaning schedule?
options: Leave it to whoever notices dirt
Wipe every area with the same cloth every day
Assign a frequency and responsible person for each location
rst-1-q031.explanation: Planned cleaning specifies locations and daily or periodic frequencies, preventing missed tasks and contamination between zones.

rst-1-q032.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q032.stem: Which operation finishes a dish by mixing cold vegetables and seasonings?
rst-1-q032.explanation: Dressing or mixing is not itself a heating step. Hygiene of utensils and ingredients must be ensured separately.

rst-1-q033.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q033.stem: A customer reports a hard foreign object in the food. What should you do?
options: Throw away only the object and return the food
Ask them to stop eating and report to the person in charge
Dispose of everything without preserving evidence
Explain that cooking makes it safe
rst-1-q033.explanation: Check for injury and establish the facts. Follow the restaurant’s response procedure, including preserving the object and food.

rst-1-q034.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q034.stem: What corrects the claim that refrigeration allows food to be used after its use-by date?
options: The date depends only on package color
Food lasts forever at low temperatures
Bacteria may still grow at low temperatures, so dates must also be observed
rst-1-q034.explanation: Refrigeration slows growth; it is not sterilization. Both storage conditions and use-by limits matter.

rst-1-q035.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q035.stem: What cut slices a long green onion from the end into thin rings?
rst-1-q035.explanation: Koguchi-giri cuts long, thin vegetables into thin rings. It differs from irregular cuts and fine chopping.

rst-1-q036.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q036.stem: You have had ongoing diarrhea since before work. What should you do?
options: Report symptoms and do not handle food
Wear double gloves and work without telling anyone
Delay reporting because it is busy
Continue if you only taste food
rst-1-q036.explanation: Concealing illness can lead to food contamination. Report first, then follow the person in charge’s instructions or seek medical attention.

rst-1-q037.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q037.stem: A customer with an egg allergy asks about sauce ingredients. What should you do?
options: Deny egg is present if it does not look yellow
Say a small amount is harmless
Say cooked sauce cannot contain egg
rst-1-q037.explanation: Allergens cannot be identified by appearance or whether food was cooked. Verify accurate information and refer uncertainties to the person in charge.

rst-1-q038.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q038.stem: Purchased tuna was left in the kitchen for a long time. What is appropriate?
options: Use it because heating always makes it safe
Report the time left out and condition, and ask for a use decision
Use it because marinating in soy sauce makes it safe
Use it unconditionally if the color looks good
rst-1-q038.explanation: Poor temperature control can create hazards such as histamine. Heating or seasoning alone does not establish safety.

rst-1-q039.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q039.stem: A customer arrives with an assistance dog. What is the appropriate basic approach?
options: Treat it exactly like an ordinary pet
Move the dog without speaking to its user
Accommodate its entry as an assistance dog
rst-1-q039.explanation: Assistance dogs perform a role. Follow the restaurant’s checking procedure and respond without obstructing the person’s use.

rst-1-q040.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q040.stem: Which bacterium may pass from a wound on the hand to food?
rst-1-q040.explanation: Staphylococcus aureus can occur on skin and in wounds. Protecting wounds and maintaining hand hygiene are important.

rst-1-q041.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q041.stem: Which heating method is used for dishes in containers, such as chawanmushi?
rst-1-q041.explanation: Steaming uses heat from water vapor. It can also cook liquid ingredients placed in containers.

rst-1-q042.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q042.stem: Which method heats ingredients in a large quantity of water or hot water?
rst-1-q042.explanation: Boiling uses water or hot water as the heating medium. Mixing and rolling are operations without heating.

rst-1-q043.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q043.stem: While preparing fish to be eaten raw, you find something resembling a parasite. What should you do?
options: Add vinegar and serve it unchanged
Stop and check with the person in charge
Sprinkle salt and consider it sufficient
Move it to a less visible part
rst-1-q043.explanation: Vinegar or salt alone cannot replace appropriate Anisakis control. Report the finding and have it handled properly.

rst-1-q044.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q044.stem: How should a toilet-cleaning brush be handled?
options: Share it with the preparation-table brush
Wash it and use it for vegetables
Dry it on a food shelf
Keep it separate and exclusively for toilets
rst-1-q044.explanation: Separate toilet tools from food-area tools to prevent bringing contamination into food-handling areas.

rst-1-q045.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q045.stem: A container of decanted detergent has no label. What should you do?
options: Do not use it until the contents are identified
Assume it is water and use it for cooking
Decide the chemical name from smell alone
Leave it on a food shelf and wait
rst-1-q045.explanation: Unlabeled chemicals risk misuse. Enforce dedicated containers, content labels, and designated storage locations.

rst-1-q046.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q046.stem: Clean tools are stored in different places each time, increasing search time. What is the improvement?
options: Only add more people to search
Set storage locations and return tools after use
rst-1-q046.explanation: Orderliness means defining storage places and returning items. It reduces wasted searching and mix-ups.

rst-1-q047.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q047.stem: How should you hold a glass when carrying it?
options: Cover the drinking edge with your hand
Hold the lower part, avoiding the drinking rim
Set the base on the dining-room floor
rst-1-q047.explanation: Keep fingers off the drinking rim to maintain hygiene and place the glass down gently.

rst-1-q048.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q048.stem: A customer requests vegan food. What should you check first?
options: Ingredients they avoid and what the restaurant can accommodate
Assume removing meat is always enough
rst-1-q048.explanation: Confirm their wishes, including eggs, dairy, and stocks. Do not make uniform assumptions about dietary restrictions.

rst-1-q049.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q049.stem: Long hair is hanging outside a hat. What is appropriate?
options: Keep touching the hair while cooking
Secure the hair to prevent it entering food
Leave it unless it falls into a dish
Remove the hat and continue working
rst-1-q049.explanation: Personal grooming also prevents foreign objects entering food. Tie up hair and maintain cleanliness before handling food.

rst-1-q050.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q050.stem: What is appropriate when controlling a dish that is cooled and reheated?
options: Allow unlimited repeated storage at room temperature
rst-1-q050.explanation: Each stage of repeated heating and cooling can involve hazards, so control the whole process.

rst-1-q051.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q051.stem: Delivered milk has torn packaging. What should you do?
options: Do not use it; report to the person in charge
Transfer it to another container and use it
Accept it if there is no smell
Check only the delivery slip and store it
rst-1-q051.explanation: Damaged packaging may allow contamination. Quantity or smell alone cannot establish safety.

rst-1-q052.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q052.stem: Why include responses to abnormalities in the hygiene management plan?
options: To always use up defective products
To respond without hesitation when a problem occurs
To remove the need for staff judgment
rst-1-q052.explanation: Defining reporting contacts and measures in advance aligns responses, but the actual situation still needs to be checked.

rst-1-q053.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q053.stem: You receive a phone question you cannot answer. What is appropriate?
options: Confirm the request and contact details, then refer it to the responsible staff
rst-1-q053.explanation: Do not give uncertain answers. Leave a note and arrange an accurate answer from the person in charge or responsible staff.

rst-1-q054.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q054.stem: A slicer is jammed. What is necessary before cleaning?
options: Stop operation and check the safety procedure
Put fingers in while it rotates
Operate it with the safety cover removed
Bring your face close to the blade
rst-1-q054.explanation: For clearing jams or cleaning, follow the machine’s prescribed safety measures, including stopping it, to prevent entanglement and cuts.

rst-1-q055.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q055.stem: A customer asks to take leftovers home. What is appropriate?
options: Check and explain the restaurant’s hygiene policy
Say it can stay at room temperature overnight
rst-1-q055.explanation: Takeaway has risks depending on food and storage conditions. Do not independently guarantee safety.

rst-1-q056.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q056.stem: A group includes someone planning to drive. How should you respond?
options: Identify the driver and do not serve them alcohol
Say driving after drinking is fine after a meal
Do not check the driver’s order
rst-1-q056.explanation: Avoid serving alcohol to anyone planning to drive. A small amount or a meal does not guarantee safe driving.

rst-1-q057.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q057.stem: What is an appropriate first response to an arriving customer?
options: Face them and greet them warmly
rst-1-q057.explanation: The greeting is the first point of contact. Direct your attention to the customer and convey a welcome.

rst-1-q058.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q058.stem: You have made a dish served cold. How should it be held until service?
options: Store it under the specified chilled conditions
Leave it at the edge of a warm preparation table
Leave it waiting in the dining area for a long time
Skip records if it feels cold to the touch
rst-1-q058.explanation: Continue appropriate refrigeration for food served without heating. Touch alone cannot replace the required controls.

rst-1-q059.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q059.stem: You need to leave your station while using a flame. What should you do?
options: Leave without telling anyone if it is on low heat
Cover the pan with combustible material and leave
Stop safely or make a reliable handover
Only check occasionally from the dining area
rst-1-q059.explanation: Do not leave a heat source unattended. Turn it off or hand it over reliably according to restaurant procedures.

rst-1-q060.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q060.stem: Which ingredient is an example associated with umami?
rst-1-q060.explanation: The textbook uses kombu stock and bonito flakes as examples of umami. Distinguish it from sweetness, sourness, and saltiness.

rst-1-q061.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q061.stem: You are cooling a large pot of stew for storage. What is appropriate?
options: Leave the entire pot at room temperature overnight
Close the lid and only turn off warming
Judge by smell the next morning
Divide it into smaller portions and cool promptly using restaurant procedures
rst-1-q061.explanation: Slow cooling after cooking can allow bacteria to multiply. Cool promptly using measures such as dividing into smaller portions.

rst-1-q062.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q062.stem: While cleaning a table, you find dirt on the outside of a condiment container. What should you do?
options: Put it back if contents remain
Turn the dirty side away to hide it
Clean it and arrange it hygienically under restaurant procedures
rst-1-q062.explanation: Tabletop supplies affect both cleanliness and hygiene. Moving or concealing dirt does not improve the problem.

rst-1-q063.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q063.stem: What should you do to limit browning of cut burdock root?
options: Soak in water or another suitable liquid according to the recipe
Leave it exposed to air for a long time
Blow dry warm air on it
Wait until the next day at room temperature
rst-1-q063.explanation: Cut-surface discoloration involves reactions with oxygen. Use suitable soaking methods for the vegetable and avoid unnecessary delay.

rst-1-q064.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q064.stem: Oil is spilled on the floor. What is an appropriate initial response?
options: Spread it with your shoe and wait for drying
Leave it until night because it is busy
Hide it under cardboard and walk over it
Alert others, prevent passage, and clean it up
rst-1-q064.explanation: Immediately reduce the slipping hazard and remove the oil under restaurant procedures. Concealing it alone cannot prevent recurrence or falls.

rst-1-q065.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q065.stem: A different fish species from the one ordered was delivered. What should you do first?
options: Accept it because the quantity matches
Compare the order and actual goods, and confirm the discrepancy
Change only the item name on the delivery slip yourself
Use it as equivalent once cooked
rst-1-q065.explanation: Receiving checks cover product identity as well as quantity. Do not substitute on your own; check with the person in charge or supplier.

rst-1-q066.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q066.stem: How should you assist a customer who finds small print hard to read?
options: Read at the same speed used for young people
Tell them nothing can be done
Offer a menu with larger print or similar assistance
Decide the order entirely for them
rst-1-q066.explanation: Provide a way for the customer to understand the information and support their own choice.

rst-1-q067.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q067.stem: A customer suddenly becomes unwell. What is the basic response?
options: Move them to another seat and leave them
Notify the person in charge and arrange necessary assistance
rst-1-q067.explanation: Check symptoms and call for support. Staff should not give medicine on their own judgment or delay responding.

rst-1-q068.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q068.stem: A customer complains that food is taking too long. What should you do first?
options: Insist it is the kitchen’s fault
Listen, check the situation, and apologize
rst-1-q068.explanation: First acknowledge the dissatisfaction and check facts. Blame-shifting and ignoring prevent understanding and resolution.

rst-1-q069.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q069.stem: Which is an appropriate characteristic of chicken breast?
options: It is always tougher than beef
It is relatively low in fat
It is guaranteed safe to eat raw
rst-1-q069.explanation: Characteristics of cuts help with recipe choices, but meat type or cut cannot establish safety for eating raw.

rst-1-q070.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q070.stem: Why mainly check the quantity needed before preparation?
options: Prepare the needed amount and reduce unnecessary removal from storage
Place all ingredients at room temperature
rst-1-q070.explanation: Calculate quantities and prepare the required ingredients. Taking out too much or leaving it out can also reduce quality.

rst-1-q071.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q071.stem: Unused broken containers occupy a worktable. Which action is the sorting step of 5S?
options: Assess need and remove unnecessary items
Leave them and attach a warning
rst-1-q071.explanation: Sorting separates necessary from unnecessary items and removes the latter. Defining storage locations is setting in order.

rst-1-q072.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q072.stem: What should you do before carrying a hot pot through a narrow aisle?
options: Call out to others and check the passage is safe
Hold the pot above your head
rst-1-q072.explanation: Prevent contact and falls when carrying hot items. Checking surroundings matters more than rushing.

rst-1-q073.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q073.stem: Which equipment supports several heating methods, such as roasting and steaming?
rst-1-q073.explanation: A steam convection oven cooks with hot air and steam. Its purpose differs from cooling or weighing equipment.

rst-1-q074.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q074.stem: Which bacterium is a concern when a large batch of curry cools slowly?
rst-1-q074.explanation: Clostridium perfringens can be a problem in stews and similar foods. Prompt cooling after cooking is a control measure.

rst-1-q075.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q075.stem: What is the problem with placing washed dishes on an unhygienic surface?
options: The washed dishes become contaminated again
rst-1-q075.explanation: If the storage surface is unhygienic, dishes can be recontaminated after washing.

rst-1-q076.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q076.stem: You have a small wound on your hand. What should you do before handling food?
options: Put food directly against the wound
Report it, protect it, and follow restaurant procedures
Use only gloves without washing hands
Tell nobody if the wound is small
rst-1-q076.explanation: Wounds can be contamination sources. Along with protection and gloves, handwashing and checking work assignments are necessary.

rst-1-q077.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q077.stem: Which tool measures a set volume of liquid?
rst-1-q077.explanation: A measuring cup measures volume. A skimmer or cooking chopsticks cannot control volume accurately.

rst-1-q078.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q078.stem: A customer drops a fork on the floor. What is appropriate?
options: Pick it up and return it without wiping
Give them a clean replacement fork
Make the customer go and wash it
Ask them to keep using it
rst-1-q078.explanation: Quickly provide a replacement. Do not have the customer reuse a dropped utensil unchanged.

rst-1-q079.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q079.stem: Which storage method prevents raw-meat juices dripping onto food below?
options: Leave it open on the top shelf
Put it beside vegetables in only a paper bag
Use a lidded container on a lower shelf
rst-1-q079.explanation: A closable container and lower-shelf storage reduce routes for meat juices to reach other food.

rst-1-q080.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q080.stem: What is needed after making a hygiene management plan?
options: Implement it and record check results
rst-1-q080.explanation: The HACCP approach requires implementing the plan, keeping records, and confirming responses when problems arise.

rst-1-q081.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q081.stem: Which pork cut has alternating layers of lean meat and fat?
rst-1-q081.explanation: Pork belly has layers of lean and fat. Choose dishes according to fat content and tissue characteristics.

rst-1-q082.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q082.stem: For norovirus control, which toilet areas are especially important to clean?
rst-1-q082.explanation: Frequently touched surfaces can transfer contamination, so include them in toilet cleaning and disinfection.

rst-1-q083.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q083.stem: Which characteristic of chicken wings is stated in the textbook?
options: They have the least fat of all chicken parts
rst-1-q083.explanation: Wings are described as rich in collagen. Check characteristics of the cut separately from safe food handling.

rst-1-q084.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q084.stem: Insecticide was used near food. What is appropriate?
options: Heat and use all of it
Wait until the smell disappears and use it
Separate nearby food and report to the person in charge
Mix it into the bottom of a dish
rst-1-q084.explanation: Chemical contamination may have occurred. Heating or smell alone cannot establish safety.

rst-1-q085.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q085.stem: What information should you give when handing over takeaway food?
options: Storage methods and precautions before eating
rst-1-q085.explanation: For safety after takeaway, give restaurant guidance suited to the dish, such as storage conditions and recommended eating times.

rst-1-q086.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q086.stem: A small glass fragment lies near a preparation table. What type of food hazard is this?
rst-1-q086.explanation: Glass is a physical foreign object that must not enter food. Also check its possible effect on nearby food.

rst-1-q087.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q087.stem: A washed cloth was left wet in a dirty place. What should you do before reuse?
options: Only wring it out and use it for dishes
Use it until it gives food a smell
Hide it wrapped in work clothes
Make it hygienically clean again and store it properly
rst-1-q087.explanation: Prevent recontamination after washing. Do not reuse a wet cloth that has been stored in an unhygienic place without treating it again.

rst-1-q088.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q088.stem: Checking a frozen-food delivery is taking time. What is appropriate?
options: Check promptly and move items to appropriate storage
Leave all products lined up at room temperature
Put everything into the freezer without checking
Warm the products to check packaging
rst-1-q088.explanation: Do not skip necessary receiving checks, but minimize time chilled and frozen products spend at room temperature.

rst-1-q089.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q089.stem: A container of cooled food has no date label. What should you do?
options: Guess and write the newest date
Use it if it smells good
Check its history and do not use it while uncertain
Copy the date from another container
rst-1-q089.explanation: Unknown storage history or expiry prevents proper control. Do not guess dates.

rst-1-q090.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q090.stem: You could not hear the date and time of a telephone reservation. What should you do?
options: Politely ask again and repeat it back
rst-1-q090.explanation: Clarify information you could not hear and repeat important details such as date, time, and party size to prevent errors.

rst-1-q091.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q091.stem: A cooking check is below the required standard. What should you do?
options: Apply additional cooking and recheck according to restaurant procedures
rst-1-q091.explanation: If cooking does not meet the standard, apply the specified additional heating or other measures and check the center before deciding.

rst-1-q092.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q092.stem: Which statement about choosing seasonal ingredients is appropriate?
options: Their season always starts on the same day nationwide
The season may vary by region and climate
Seasonal food needs no storage control
rst-1-q092.explanation: Seasonality varies with region and climate. Freshness at delivery and storage conditions must also be checked.

rst-1-q093.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q093.stem: An instruction specifies measuring an ingredient by weight. Which tool is suitable?
rst-1-q093.explanation: Use a scale for weight. Distinguish it from tools measuring volume or temperature.

rst-1-q094.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q094.stem: A carrot is cut into pieces half the size of a half-moon slice. What is the cut?
rst-1-q094.explanation: Halving a circular slice makes a half-moon; halving it again makes a quarter-round, or icho-giri.

rst-1-q095.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q095.stem: A raw-meat container’s lid is not closed. What is appropriate?
options: Cover it by putting vegetables on top
Only move it to a high shelf
Check for spread of contamination and restore proper storage
rst-1-q095.explanation: Prevent leaks and check nearby food. Moving it higher may contaminate food below.

rst-1-q096.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q096.stem: You took salad out earlier than intended instead of just before service. What should you do?
options: Check time left out and other conditions, then consult the person in charge
Assume surrounding it with ice makes history irrelevant
Assume changing the plate makes it safe
rst-1-q096.explanation: If a non-heated dish leaves chilled control, check time and condition instead of deciding safety on your own.

rst-1-q097.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q097.stem: Cooked rice has a different firmness each time. What should you check first?
options: Only the order of plating after cooking
The balance of rice and water quantities
Only the location of the warming container
rst-1-q097.explanation: Rice and water quantities affect the cooked texture. Check measurement and the prescribed rice-cooking procedure.

rst-1-q098.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q098.stem: A customer asks about halal options, but seasoning information is unavailable. What should you do?
options: Claim compliance if no pork is visible
Decide they can eat it from nationality alone
Check ingredients and the conditions the restaurant can meet
Guarantee compliance if all alcohol is cooked off
rst-1-q098.explanation: Halal requests involve ingredients and cooking conditions. Check the customer’s requirements and restaurant information; do not give casual guarantees.

rst-1-q099.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q099.stem: A customer is dissatisfied because service did not meet expectations based on price. Which relationship matters?
options: The gap between expectations and actual experience
rst-1-q099.explanation: Customer satisfaction relates to expectations before the visit and actual experience. Price and atmosphere also influence expectations.

rst-1-q100.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q100.stem: A stir-fry turned watery after too much food was added at once. How should it be improved?
options: Cook quantities suited to the equipment’s capacity
Stack plates to hide the moisture
rst-1-q100.explanation: Overloading lowers the temperature and makes adequate heating and the desired stir-fried texture harder to achieve.

rst-1-q101.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q101.stem: Which beef cut matches the textbook description of tender and relatively low in fat?
rst-1-q101.explanation: Tenderloin is described as fine-textured, tender, and low in fat. Choose cuts suited to the dish.

rst-1-q102.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q102.stem: You are placing heavy dishes and tall glasses on a tray. What is appropriate?
options: Always put heavy items at the far edge
Arrange them with a stable center of gravity to resist tipping
Carry above your head without checking contents
rst-1-q102.explanation: Consider placement of heavy and tall items, prioritizing tray stability and avoiding contact with surroundings.

rst-1-q103.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q103.stem: You finely chop an onion so it mixes into a dish. What is the cut?
rst-1-q103.explanation: Mincing chops into fine pieces. Distinguish it from baton cuts and other shapes.

rst-1-q104.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q104.stem: Which foods can present a Salmonella risk when handling raw animal products?
options: Only the outside of canned-food boxes
rst-1-q104.explanation: Salmonella can occur in the intestines of livestock and poultry, and meat or eggs may be contaminated.

rst-1-q105.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q105.stem: After cleaning, you sit in a customer seat and notice dirt under the table. What next?
options: Recheck cleanliness from the customer’s viewpoint
Leave it if invisible when standing
Hide it by seating people in a dark place
rst-1-q105.explanation: What is visible from customer seats also affects perceived cleanliness. Checking from the user’s position reduces oversights.

rst-1-q106.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q106.stem: Allergen ingredient information cannot be found immediately. What is appropriate?
options: Say a small amount is fine
Explain that it is uncertain and check with the person in charge
Assert an answer from memory alone
Judge only from the food photo
rst-1-q106.explanation: Stating uncertain information as fact can cause serious health harm. Refer to someone who can verify it.

rst-1-q107.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q107.stem: What should you do when preparing a child’s seat?
options: Check the guardian’s wishes and surrounding safety
Always place it in the route for hot dishes
Seat the child alone far away
Put all equipment on the floor
rst-1-q107.explanation: Consider the child’s movement and surroundings, and consult the guardian to provide a convenient, safe seat.

rst-1-q108.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q108.stem: Which method grills food by applying flame or heat directly?
rst-1-q108.explanation: Direct-flame grilling exposes food directly to flame or heat, unlike cooking through a griddle or similar surface.

rst-1-q109.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q109.stem: You are storing cooked rice for fried rice. What is appropriate?
options: Cooked rice lasts forever at room temperature
Spices remove the need for control
Control temperature and time even after cooking
rst-1-q109.explanation: Bacillus cereus and other hazards associated with grains require attention. Cooking alone does not guarantee storage safety.

rst-1-q110.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q110.stem: Which method does the textbook show for preventing cut apples from browning?
options: Expose to hot air for a long time
Leave overnight in a bright place
rst-1-q110.explanation: The textbook gives salt-water treatment for apples and pears. Choose methods suited to each ingredient and recipe.

rst-1-q111.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q111.stem: A refrigerator has no thermometer and is checked only by touch. What should you do?
options: Assume cold airflow means normal operation
Tell the person in charge and arrange temperature measurement
Judge by the outside door color
Record how often food is touched
rst-1-q111.explanation: Temperature control needs objective checks. Touch or airflow alone cannot confirm the internal temperature.

rst-1-q112.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q112.stem: A glass is on a Chinese restaurant’s rotating table. What should you do?
options: Spin it forcefully toward the edge
Put a heavy plate on it
Leave the area and ignore it
Check safety and guide the customer to move it to the fixed table
rst-1-q112.explanation: Personal chopsticks or glasses on a rotating table can cause collisions. Give safe guidance under restaurant procedures.

rst-1-q113.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q113.stem: You missed between your fingers and your thumbs while washing hands. What should you do?
options: Dry only the palms and finish
Repeat the procedure so no areas are missed
Put on gloves instead of rewashing
rst-1-q113.explanation: Handwashing must cover more than palms, including finger webs, thumbs, fingertips, and wrists.

rst-1-q114.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q114.stem: A customer orders a sold-out item. What is appropriate?
options: Silently replace it with another item
Pretend you did not hear the order
Wait until payment to say it is unavailable
rst-1-q114.explanation: Clearly explain the shortage and offer alternatives the customer can choose. Do not change the item on your own.

rst-1-q115.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q115.stem: Someone is about to handle food wearing a ring. What is appropriate?
options: Move the ring outside the glove
Remove it under restaurant hygiene rules
Allow it freely unless it falls into food
rst-1-q115.explanation: Jewelry can cause foreign-object contamination or carry dirt. Address it in grooming checks before food handling.

rst-1-q116.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe handling of equipment.
rst-1-q116.stem: Why does shaping sushi need particular care?
options: Vinegared rice removes the need for clean tools
It often has no heating step after shaping
rst-1-q116.explanation: For dishes without heating after shaping, preventing contamination from hands and equipment is especially important.

rst-1-q117.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q117.stem: A knife and fork are positioned to suggest the meal is still in progress. What should you do before clearing?
options: Check the meal’s progress and the customer’s wishes
Throw and collect just one utensil
Do not observe until the seat is empty
rst-1-q117.explanation: Utensil placement is a clue to meal progress, but also check the actual situation and customer’s wishes.

rst-1-q118.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q118.stem: You find and immediately correct a hygiene problem. What should you record?
options: Only “no abnormality” because it was fixed
Change discovery time to the previous day
rst-1-q118.explanation: Recording the abnormality and corrective action even after correction supports recurrence prevention and cause investigation.

rst-1-q119.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-1-q119.stem: Tools are not returned after cleaning and soon become scattered. What is needed under 5S?
options: Have only assigned staff search for tools
Build the habit of following agreed rules
rst-1-q119.explanation: Sorting, setting in order, and cleaning once is insufficient. Correct behavior must become a continuing habit.

rst-1-q120.objective: Choose customer service appropriate to the customer’s situation.
rst-1-q120.stem: What is appropriate for a polite bow?
options: Swing only your neck while walking
Stop and straighten your posture before bowing
Bow backward without looking toward the customer
rst-1-q120.explanation: Be aware of posture and procedure, and bow in a safe state. Bowing is more than moving the neck.

rst-1-q121.objective: Classify food hazards, and stop use and report abnormalities.
rst-1-q121.stem: How is food poisoning caused by detergent residue classified?
rst-1-q121.explanation: Harm from chemicals such as detergent is distinguished from harm caused by microbes or parasites.

rst-1-q122.objective: Use meat fat and connective-tissue characteristics to choose cutting and heating methods.
rst-1-q122.stem: Why is beef shoulder suitable as a soup ingredient?
options: It contains no fat at all
It is the most tender of all cuts
It contains abundant extractives and collagen
rst-1-q122.explanation: Shoulder is fairly firm and lean, with extractives and collagen that suit stews and soups.

rst-1-q123.objective: Observe food, service, cleanliness, and atmosphere, and choose improvements.
rst-1-q123.stem: What does C in QSCA mainly represent?
options: Cleanliness of the restaurant and employees
rst-1-q123.explanation: C means Cleanliness, including cleaning, organization, and employee grooming.

rst-1-q124.objective: Apply the three principles of bacterial food-poisoning prevention across the workflow.
rst-1-q124.stem: What is the main preventive role of chilled storage and storage-time control?
rst-1-q124.explanation: Low temperatures and time control suppress growth; they differ from killing bacteria or removing foreign objects.

rst-1-q125.objective: Use meat fat and connective-tissue characteristics to choose cutting and heating methods.
rst-1-q125.stem: Before using pork collar for ginger pork, which preparation should be checked?
options: Divide the bone into three pieces
rst-1-q125.explanation: The textbook shows cutting through the connective tissue in pork collar before cooking.

rst-1-q126.objective: Observe food, service, cleanliness, and atmosphere, and choose improvements.
rst-1-q126.stem: Which describes serving at the appropriate temperature?
options: Serve all dishes at room temperature
Serve hot and cold dishes in their respective appropriate conditions
rst-1-q126.explanation: Appropriate temperature suits the dish; it does not mean one temperature for everything.

rst-1-q127.objective: Understand sources of major bacteria and choose prevention suited to food and tasks.
rst-1-q127.stem: Which bacterium originates in cattle or pig intestines and can cause bloody diarrhea through a potent toxin?
rst-1-q127.explanation: Enterohemorrhagic E. coli can contaminate meat and cause food poisoning when cooking is inadequate.

rst-1-q128.objective: Use meat fat and connective-tissue characteristics to choose cutting and heating methods.
rst-1-q128.stem: Which statement about pork tenderloin is appropriate?
options: Alternating layers of lean and fat
A cut consisting only of skin
The most sinewy cut, exclusively for stewing
rst-1-q128.explanation: Pork tenderloin is fine-textured, tender, and low in fat.

rst-1-q129.objective: Observe food, service, cleanliness, and atmosphere, and choose improvements.
rst-1-q129.stem: Which QSCA element combines restaurant appearance and employee attitudes?
rst-1-q129.explanation: Atmosphere comprises physical aspects such as facilities and nonphysical aspects such as service attitudes.

rst-1-q130.objective: Understand sources of major bacteria and choose prevention suited to food and tasks.
rst-1-q130.stem: Which combination is shown as a main source of Bacillus cereus?
rst-1-q130.explanation: Bacillus cereus is widespread in nature; grains and beans that may carry soil can be sources.

rst-1-q131.objective: Use meat fat and connective-tissue characteristics to choose cutting and heating methods.
rst-1-q131.stem: Which comparison of chicken thigh and breast is appropriate?
options: Thigh has fat and rich flavor
Thigh has the least fat of all chicken parts
Thigh and breast always have equal fat
rst-1-q131.explanation: Chicken thigh has fat and richness. Use cut characteristics when choosing dishes.

rst-1-q132.objective: Express welcome and apology with clean grooming and calm movements.
rst-1-q132.stem: What posture is appropriate when standing in an aisle during service?
options: Lean against the wall with arms folded
Stand straight and pay attention to the dining area
rst-1-q132.explanation: Maintain posture and attend to customers so you can respond when needed. Avoid staring.

rst-1-q133.objective: Understand sources of major bacteria and choose prevention suited to food and tasks.
rst-1-q133.stem: Which characteristic of Clostridium perfringens is shown?
options: It grows without oxygen and forms spores
rst-1-q133.explanation: It forms spores and grows in low-oxygen conditions, making cooling after large-scale cooking important.

rst-1-q134.objective: Identify fish parts as instructed and explain seasons including regional differences.
rst-1-q134.stem: What is the line-shaped part running along both sides of a fish’s body?
rst-1-q134.explanation: The lateral line runs along the fish’s side and is distinct from gill covers and fins.

rst-1-q135.objective: Express welcome and apology with clean grooming and calm movements.
rst-1-q135.stem: What approximate angle does the textbook give for a light bow, eshaku?
rst-1-q135.explanation: Eshaku is about 15 degrees and is used, for example, when passing someone or asking them to wait.

rst-1-q136.objective: Understand sources of major bacteria and choose prevention suited to food and tasks.
rst-1-q136.stem: Which environment is particularly associated with Vibrio parahaemolyticus?
rst-1-q136.explanation: It lives in seawater and similar environments and can contaminate seafood.

rst-1-q137.objective: Identify fish parts as instructed and explain seasons including regional differences.
rst-1-q137.stem: Which seafood combination is classified as a spring-season example?
rst-1-q137.explanation: The textbook’s spring examples include Spanish mackerel and clams. Consider regional and climatic variation.

rst-1-q138.objective: Express welcome and apology with clean grooming and calm movements.
rst-1-q138.stem: Which basic bow welcomes customers or expresses thanks at payment?
options: A light bow with your back turned
rst-1-q138.explanation: The textbook uses a keirei bow of about 30 degrees for welcome or thanks at payment.

rst-1-q139.objective: Explain why ordinary heating or refrigeration alone cannot establish safety for hazards other than bacteria.
rst-1-q139.stem: Which route can bring norovirus into the kitchen?
options: Hands contaminated through an infected person’s feces or vomit
rst-1-q139.explanation: Norovirus spreads through feces or vomit, making health management and handwashing important.

rst-1-q140.objective: Identify fish parts as instructed and explain seasons including regional differences.
rst-1-q140.stem: Which seafood is classified as a winter-season example?
rst-1-q140.explanation: The textbook lists yellowtail as a winter example. Seasons may vary by production area and other conditions.

rst-1-q141.objective: Express welcome and apology with clean grooming and calm movements.
rst-1-q141.stem: What approximate angle is used for the deepest respectful bow in a formal apology?
rst-1-q141.explanation: The textbook gives about 45 degrees for saikeirei, used for apologies or farewells.

rst-1-q142.objective: Explain why ordinary heating or refrigeration alone cannot establish safety for hazards other than bacteria.
rst-1-q142.stem: Why does temperature control of red-fleshed fish require attention to histamine?
options: Fresh fish always contains large amounts
It may increase with poor storage
It arises only when fish is cut
rst-1-q142.explanation: Histamine can increase during improper storage of red-fleshed fish, so chilled control matters from receiving onward.

rst-1-q143.objective: Use major vegetable categories and seasonal guides to check ingredients and explain them.
rst-1-q143.stem: How are Chinese cabbage, green onions, and spinach classified?
rst-1-q143.explanation: These vegetables are classified as leaf-and-stem vegetables because leaves or stems are mainly used.

rst-1-q144.objective: Express welcome and apology with clean grooming and calm movements.
rst-1-q144.stem: Which bowing posture is better than bending only the neck?
options: Nod only the head while walking
Incline the upper body while keeping the back straight
Arch the lower back and raise the chin
rst-1-q144.explanation: Prepare your posture and incline the upper body politely, rather than only the neck.

rst-1-q145.objective: Explain why ordinary heating or refrigeration alone cannot establish safety for hazards other than bacteria.
rst-1-q145.stem: Why remove fish viscera promptly for Anisakis control?
options: All fish bacteria exist only in viscera
rst-1-q145.explanation: Viscera may contain Anisakis, so remove them promptly, while still carrying out other controls and checks.

rst-1-q146.objective: Use major vegetable categories and seasonal guides to check ingredients and explain them.
rst-1-q146.stem: Which combination matches the textbook’s fruit-like vegetable category?
rst-1-q146.explanation: The textbook classifies strawberries, melons, and watermelons as fruit-like vegetables.

rst-1-q147.objective: Check where to hold tableware and its center of gravity to carry food steadily.
rst-1-q147.stem: What is the basic way to support a tray?
options: Pinch one rim point with fingertips alone
Support its center with the non-dominant hand
rst-1-q147.explanation: Support near the center with the palm and spread the fingers for stability.

rst-1-q148.objective: Explain why ordinary heating or refrigeration alone cannot establish safety for hazards other than bacteria.
rst-1-q148.stem: Which belief about parasite control in raw fish is incorrect?
rst-1-q148.explanation: Ordinary vinegar curing does not necessarily reliably kill Anisakis.

rst-1-q149.objective: Use major vegetable categories and seasonal guides to check ingredients and explain them.
rst-1-q149.stem: Which vegetables match a winter-season example?
rst-1-q149.explanation: The textbook lists Chinese cabbage and daikon as winter examples.

rst-1-q150.objective: Check where to hold tableware and its center of gravity to carry food steadily.
rst-1-q150.stem: What is the basic way to carry an empty tray?
options: Wave it at customer face height
Hold it at your side with the non-dominant hand
rst-1-q150.explanation: Hold an empty tray at the side with the non-dominant hand and avoid hitting surroundings.

rst-1-q151.objective: Check both order details and hygiene condition, and separate nonconforming goods.
rst-1-q151.stem: Why mainly check storage instructions at receiving?
options: A label removes the need for visual checks
It removes the need to check the product name
Confirm required storage conditions are being met
Conclude all foods can stay at room temperature
rst-1-q151.explanation: Check storage instructions against delivery condition and storage after receiving.

rst-1-q152.objective: Prepare required quantities and prevent warming and contamination during preparation.
rst-1-q152.stem: Why mainly avoid preparing raw ingredients and plating food simultaneously on one table?
options: Prevent contamination from unprepared ingredients to finished food
Make every vegetable the same color
rst-1-q152.explanation: Separate place or time to prevent dirt and bacteria from raw ingredients reaching cooked or ready-to-eat finished food.

rst-1-q153.objective: Check where to hold tableware and its center of gravity to carry food steadily.
rst-1-q153.stem: Which direction should be checked when placing a dish?
options: Face the dish’s front toward the customer
Always face the front toward yourself
Always show the plate’s bottom to the customer
rst-1-q153.explanation: Face the food’s front toward the customer for appearance and ease of eating.

rst-1-q154.objective: Check both order details and hygiene condition, and separate nonconforming goods.
rst-1-q154.stem: Why distinguish an infrared thermometer reading from food core temperature?
options: It cannot display values for frozen goods
rst-1-q154.explanation: Use an infrared thermometer for surface temperature, not as a substitute for core temperature.

rst-1-q155.objective: Prepare required quantities and prevent warming and contamination during preparation.
rst-1-q155.stem: Which combination should you check for thawing frozen ingredients?
options: A method suited to food and packaging, plus contamination prevention
rst-1-q155.explanation: Choose thawing suited to the food and packaging, preventing warming and contamination from juices.

rst-1-q156.objective: Understand the basic one-soup, three-dish layout and service order, and serve according to restaurant policy.
rst-1-q156.stem: Where is soup placed in a basic Japanese meal setting?
options: Always at the far back center
rst-1-q156.explanation: In a basic one-soup, three-dish setting, rice is on the left and soup on the right.

rst-1-q157.objective: Check internal storage temperature, storage limits, and responses to abnormalities as one process.
rst-1-q157.stem: Why distinguish a refrigerator setting from its actual internal temperature?
options: Actual temperature may not match the setting
There can never be temperature differences inside
rst-1-q157.explanation: The setting is a target; actual temperature must be checked with a thermometer.

rst-1-q158.objective: Connect cut names to finished shapes and explain why uniform sizes matter.
rst-1-q158.stem: What shape results when a round slice is divided in two along its diameter?
rst-1-q158.explanation: A circle cut in half gives a half-moon; halving it again gives quarter-round slices.

rst-1-q159.objective: Understand the basic one-soup, three-dish layout and service order, and serve according to restaurant policy.
rst-1-q159.stem: What is the basic understanding of the honored seat in a Japanese room?
options: Always the closest seat to the entrance
Generally a comfortable and safe position
rst-1-q159.explanation: The honored seat generally means a comfortable, safe position, but also check actual wishes and ease of use.

rst-1-q160.objective: Check internal storage temperature, storage limits, and responses to abnormalities as one process.
rst-1-q160.stem: What is appropriate when recording refrigerator temperature outside the standard?
options: Write only the restored normal reading
Write the expected value without measurement
Record the abnormal value and action taken
rst-1-q160.explanation: Recording abnormalities and actions allows later checking of food impact and improvements.

rst-1-q161.objective: Connect cut names to finished shapes and explain why uniform sizes matter.
rst-1-q161.stem: Which cut makes uniform long stick-like pieces?
rst-1-q161.explanation: Hyoshigi-giri makes sticks, unlike circular slices or thin sheets.

rst-1-q162.objective: Understand the basic one-soup, three-dish layout and service order, and serve according to restaurant policy.
rst-1-q162.stem: When is fruit, mizugashi, basically served in a Japanese kaiseki meal?
rst-1-q162.explanation: In the textbook’s basic order, fruit follows rice. Check the restaurant’s actual menu.

rst-1-q163.objective: Break routes of contamination from raw ingredients to prepared food.
rst-1-q163.stem: After washing a raw-meat board, meat juices splash onto a clean board. What is the problem?
rst-1-q163.explanation: Washed equipment becomes contaminated by meat juices. Do not use it; carry out the necessary washing and disinfection.

rst-1-q164.objective: Connect cut names to finished shapes and explain why uniform sizes matter.
rst-1-q164.stem: What cut makes long, thin, flat strips?
rst-1-q164.explanation: Tanzaku-giri makes flat rectangular strips, distinct from sticks or cubes.

rst-1-q165.objective: Understand the basic one-soup, three-dish layout and service order, and serve according to restaurant policy.
rst-1-q165.stem: What should you prepare for several people sharing a large Japanese dish?
options: Small sharing plates and necessary utensils
rst-1-q165.explanation: Prepare clean utensils and small plates so food can be divided from the large dish.

rst-1-q166.objective: Break routes of contamination from raw ingredients to prepared food.
rst-1-q166.stem: Why assign refrigerator storage positions by food type?
options: Make contamination through drips and contact easier to control
rst-1-q166.explanation: Separation by type supports contamination prevention and storage-condition checks.

rst-1-q167.objective: Connect cut names to finished shapes and explain why uniform sizes matter.
rst-1-q167.explanation: Sainome-giri makes cubes, unlike angular thin slices.

rst-1-q168.objective: Check cutlery placement and respond without assuming whether the meal is finished.
rst-1-q168.stem: How should a knife be set in a basic Western place setting?
options: On the right with the blade facing inward
On the left with the blade facing outward
Upright in the center with the edge up
With the blade inside a glass
rst-1-q168.explanation: The basic position is right side, blade inward. Check safety and ease of use.

rst-1-q169.objective: Remove dirt before proper disinfection and prevent chemical mix-ups.
rst-1-q169.stem: What is appropriate after washing, rinsing, and disinfecting tools?
options: Lay them on a wet floor
Dry and store them in a clean place
Wipe moisture with a dirty cloth
rst-1-q169.explanation: Drying and clean storage are also required to prevent recontamination after treatment.

rst-1-q170.objective: Connect cut names to finished shapes and explain why uniform sizes matter.
rst-1-q170.stem: Which comparison of arare-giri and sainome-giri is appropriate?
rst-1-q170.explanation: Arare-giri is classified as smaller than regular dice and larger than mince.

rst-1-q171.objective: Check cutlery placement and respond without assuming whether the meal is finished.
rst-1-q171.stem: How should multiple course knives and forks be arranged?
options: In order of use from outside inward
Stack all handles on the plate
Put the most expensive ones in the center
rst-1-q171.explanation: Arrange course cutlery so it can be used from outside inward in serving order.

rst-1-q172.objective: Remove dirt before proper disinfection and prevent chemical mix-ups.
rst-1-q172.stem: What container is suitable for decanted chemicals?
options: A label with only a food name
A dedicated container clearly identifying its contents
rst-1-q172.explanation: Use dedicated containers and clear labels so chemicals are not mistakenly used on food.

rst-1-q173.objective: Connect cut names to finished shapes and explain why uniform sizes matter.
rst-1-q173.stem: What operation rotates daikon while peeling a thin continuous ribbon?
rst-1-q173.explanation: Katsuramuki peels daikon into a thin ribbon, distinct from chopping already-cut sheets.

rst-1-q174.objective: Check cutlery placement and respond without assuming whether the meal is finished.

Always innermost to the left of the fork

options: Equipment material and product conditions of use

rst-1-q177.objective: Check cutlery placement and respond without assuming whether the meal is finished.

options: Always over food on the plate

rst-1-q178.stem: Why separate toilet-cleaning clothes and shoes from cooking gear?
options: Avoid bringing contamination into the kitchen
rst-1-q178.explanation: Separate cleaning gear and tools to avoid carrying contamination into the kitchen.

rst-1-q179.objective: Choose browning prevention suited to the ingredient and distinguish it from hygiene treatment.
rst-1-q179.stem: What mainly causes browning on a cut vegetable surface?
options: Proteins denature from heat at the cut
rst-1-q179.explanation: Browning here is discoloration from substances reacting with oxygen; adjust oxygen contact appropriately for the ingredient.

rst-1-q180.explanation: The goblet is introduced mainly as a water glass.
