rst-1-q181.objective: Keep cleaning tools and clothing separate by use, and clean contact surfaces too.
rst-1-q181.stem: What is the basic order for washing toilet bowls and floors in the textbook?
options: Finish the floor, then wash the bowl and leave splashes
Put food on the floor before washing the bowl
Change to a kitchen brush only for the floor
Wash the bowl before the floor
rst-1-q181.explanation: The example washes and rinses the bowl, then washes the floor. Follow restaurant procedures with dedicated tools.

rst-1-q182.objective: Choose browning prevention suited to the ingredient and distinguish it from hygiene treatment.
rst-1-q182.stem: Which recipe liquid is suitable for limiting lotus-root browning?
rst-1-q182.explanation: The textbook gives vinegar-water soaking for lotus root and burdock. Follow restaurant concentration and timing procedures.

rst-1-q183.objective: Understand round-table seating and sharing basics, and prevent rotating-table accidents.
rst-1-q183.stem: Why change individual sharing plates for each Chinese dish?
rst-1-q183.explanation: Changing plates between dishes lets customers enjoy each flavor without mixing them.

rst-1-q184.objective: Keep cleaning tools and clothing separate by use, and clean contact surfaces too.
rst-1-q184.stem: How should toilet-cleaning tools be handled after washing?
options: Dry and store in a dedicated place
Put them on the salad table
rst-1-q184.explanation: Wash and dry the tools themselves, then store separately from other uses.

rst-1-q185.objective: Choose browning prevention suited to the ingredient and distinguish it from hygiene treatment.
rst-1-q185.stem: What is a correct understanding of food that did not discolor after browning prevention?
options: Color retention alone cannot establish hygiene safety
Refrigeration and expiry controls are unnecessary
It is exactly the same as chemical sterilization
rst-1-q185.explanation: Browning prevention addresses color change; it does not replace microbial controls or storage management.

rst-1-q186.objective: Understand round-table seating and sharing basics, and prevent rotating-table accidents.
rst-1-q186.stem: Which is basically the lower-status seat at a round table?
rst-1-q186.explanation: A seat near the entrance is generally lower-status at a round table too. Also check preferences and safety.

rst-1-q187.objective: Check your health and grooming and openly report abnormalities affecting food.
rst-1-q187.stem: Why mainly ask about diarrhea and vomiting during health checks?
options: There is a risk of transferring pathogens to food
rst-1-q187.explanation: Digestive symptoms in food handlers can lead to food contamination, so check before work.

rst-1-q188.objective: Identify fish processing states and check preparation required before cooking.
rst-1-q188.stem: What is fish with only the viscera removed called?
rst-1-q188.explanation: The textbook defines semi-dressed as viscera removed. Also check the supplier’s terminology.

rst-1-q189.objective: Understand round-table seating and sharing basics, and prevent rotating-table accidents.
rst-1-q189.stem: What basic rotating-table direction does the textbook show?
options: Always alternate quickly left and right
Always reverse with no set direction
rst-1-q189.explanation: The textbook gives clockwise as a general example, but prioritize others’ movements and safety checks.

rst-1-q190.objective: Check your health and grooming and openly report abnormalities affecting food.
rst-1-q190.stem: Why do apparently healthy people still need handwashing?
rst-1-q190.explanation: People may be infected without symptoms, so routine handwashing and health management remain necessary.

rst-1-q191.objective: Identify fish processing states and check preparation required before cooking.
rst-1-q191.stem: What is fish with head, gills, and viscera removed called?
rst-1-q191.explanation: The textbook defines dressed as removal of the head, gills, and viscera.

rst-1-q192.objective: Understand round-table seating and sharing basics, and prevent rotating-table accidents.
rst-1-q192.stem: Why should personal chopsticks not be put on the rotating table?
options: To give them to others as shared chopsticks
To rotate their tips toward food
Keep the moving dish area separate from personal items
To circulate them with shared food
rst-1-q192.explanation: The rotating table moves dishes; personal chopsticks and glasses should not be placed on it.

rst-1-q193.objective: Check your health and grooming and openly report abnormalities affecting food.
rst-1-q193.stem: What is a purpose of tying hair and keeping work clothes clean?
options: Prevent foreign objects and food contamination
rst-1-q193.explanation: Arrange grooming to keep hair and dirty clothes away from food and work hygienically.

rst-1-q194.objective: Identify fish processing states and check preparation required before cooking.
rst-1-q194.stem: What is an unprocessed whole fish called?
rst-1-q194.explanation: Round denotes a whole fish before processing.

rst-1-q195.objective: Ask wishes and offer appropriate guidance to families with children, older people, and people with disabilities.
rst-1-q195.stem: What posture helps when speaking with a wheelchair user?
options: Move close to the same eye level so expressions are visible
Move the wheelchair without looking at the person
rst-1-q195.explanation: Address the person directly and consider a height at which both can easily see expressions.

rst-1-q196.objective: Wash hands when changing tasks, including fingertips and thumbs without missing areas.
rst-1-q196.stem: Why wash up to the wrists during handwashing?
options: Washing only wrists removes the need for fingertips
Areas beyond palms can also be missed
rst-1-q196.explanation: Wash fingertips, thumbs, finger webs, and wrists to avoid missing areas.

rst-1-q197.objective: Identify fish processing states and check preparation required before cooking.
rst-1-q197.stem: What must the restaurant still check even when fish is labeled fillet?
options: Skip bones because the label says fillet
Judge freshness from the processing label alone
Actual processing state and remaining bones
rst-1-q197.explanation: Suppliers may define terms differently. Check actual condition and suitability for the dish.

rst-1-q198.objective: Ask wishes and offer appropriate guidance to families with children, older people, and people with disabilities.
rst-1-q198.stem: Which correctly lists types of assistance dogs?
options: Only hunting, guard, and herding dogs
Guide dogs, service dogs, and hearing dogs
rst-1-q198.explanation: Assistance dogs collectively include guide, service, and hearing dogs, distinct from ordinary pets.

rst-1-q199.objective: Wash hands when changing tasks, including fingertips and thumbs without missing areas.
rst-1-q199.stem: What is necessary after using soap for handwashing?
options: Plate food with detergent still on hands
Wipe only with a dirty towel
rst-1-q199.explanation: After washing with soap, rinse thoroughly and dry hygienically.

rst-1-q200.objective: Check rice-water quantities and boiling methods suited to ingredients for consistent quality.
rst-1-q200.stem: Why soak rice in water before cooking?
rst-1-q200.explanation: Allow water absorption before heating and manage the balance of rice and water quantities.

rst-1-q201.objective: Ask wishes and offer appropriate guidance to families with children, older people, and people with disabilities.
rst-1-q201.stem: How should you interact with an assistance dog at work?
options: Give it a snack before guiding the customer
Stroke it while pulling it to the seat
Check its user’s wishes and do not distract the dog
Move it to another room without asking
rst-1-q201.explanation: The dog is supporting its user. Do not touch it or feed it without permission; check with the user.

rst-1-q202.objective: Wash hands when changing tasks, including fingertips and thumbs without missing areas.
rst-1-q202.stem: How should you switch from handling money to plating food?
options: Wash hands and restore a clean condition
Keep the same gloves for payment and plating
Wash all at once after plating
rst-1-q202.explanation: Handwashing is needed after money handling to avoid carrying contamination into the next food task.

rst-1-q203.objective: Check rice-water quantities and boiling methods suited to ingredients for consistent quality.
rst-1-q203.stem: What effect is shown for adding vinegar to boiling water?
rst-1-q203.explanation: The textbook gives adding vinegar to boiling water as an example for making white ingredients’ color clearer.

rst-1-q204.objective: Ask wishes and offer appropriate guidance to families with children, older people, and people with disabilities.
rst-1-q204.stem: A customer showing an ear symbol requests written communication. What should you do?
options: Refuse the order without a companion
Check usable methods such as paper or a device
rst-1-q204.explanation: Check a communication method the customer understands, according to their hearing and wishes.

rst-1-q205.objective: Carry out tidying and planned cleaning, managing waste separately from food.
rst-1-q205.stem: What describes seiketsu, the cleanliness step of 5S?
options: Only selecting and discarding unnecessary items
A maintained state of sorting, order, and cleaning
rst-1-q205.explanation: Thorough sorting, setting in order, and cleaning, maintained over time, create cleanliness.

rst-1-q206.objective: Check rice-water quantities and boiling methods suited to ingredients for consistent quality.
rst-1-q206.stem: What example effect is shown for baking soda in boiling water?
rst-1-q206.explanation: The textbook gives clearer green color as an example. In practice, follow recipe and ingredient conditions.

rst-1-q207.objective: Ask wishes and offer appropriate guidance to families with children, older people, and people with disabilities.
rst-1-q207.stem: Which judgment should be avoided when choosing seating for a family with children?
options: Assume needed support from age alone
rst-1-q207.explanation: Needs vary by person and situation. Check customer or guardian wishes and safety.

rst-1-q208.objective: Carry out tidying and planned cleaning, managing waste separately from food.
rst-1-q208.stem: What is a benefit of daily, weekly, and monthly cleaning plans?
options: Reduce every location to monthly cleaning
Remove the need to check responsibility
Manage places daily work cannot reach
Leave dirt until the scheduled day regardless
rst-1-q208.explanation: Set frequency by dirt and location, planning cleaning that cannot be done routinely.

rst-1-q209.objective: Prepare required quantities and prevent warming and contamination during preparation.
rst-1-q209.stem: An ingredient uses 150g for three people. How much is needed for ten at the same portion size?
rst-1-q209.explanation: 150g ÷ 3 people × 10 people = 500g. Check required quantities from headcount and portion size before preparation.

rst-1-q210.objective: Serve promptly and accurately explain storage conditions and limits for takeaway.
rst-1-q210.stem: Why explain storage methods for takeaway food?
options: Help it be handled appropriately outside the restaurant
Give every dish the same expiry
Leave all food management to the customer
rst-1-q210.explanation: Alongside restaurant controls, accurately explain temperature and precautions before eating after takeaway.

rst-1-q211.objective: Carry out tidying and planned cleaning, managing waste separately from food.
rst-1-q211.stem: What is a basic requirement for a food-waste container?
options: Shared with a food mixing bowl
A container leaking at the bottom
A container holding ingredients being prepared
rst-1-q211.explanation: Use dedicated lidded containers for food scraps to prevent bacteria, insects, and rodents.

rst-1-q212.objective: Check oil and batch size to prevent uneven heating and burns.
rst-1-q212.stem: When checking frying-oil deterioration, which change matters?
rst-1-q212.explanation: Check oil quality each use, using changes such as foaming as judgment information.

rst-1-q213.objective: Serve promptly and accurately explain storage conditions and limits for takeaway.
rst-1-q213.stem: Why treat leftovers differently from takeaway prepared for sale?
options: Sale products need no expiry information
Time after cooking and service processes differ
rst-1-q213.explanation: Time spent at the dining table differs from a planned sale process. Check restaurant policy and hygiene conditions.

rst-1-q214.objective: Carry out tidying and planned cleaning, managing waste separately from food.
rst-1-q214.stem: Where should food-waste containers be placed?
options: On the drying shelf for clean dishes
A designated location that does not interfere with work
rst-1-q214.explanation: Separate waste locations so they do not affect food or clean equipment.

rst-1-q215.objective: Check oil and batch size to prevent uneven heating and burns.
rst-1-q215.stem: Why mainly stay at the station when cooking with hot oil?
options: Respond to overheating, fire, and other abnormalities
rst-1-q215.explanation: Do not leave a frying heat source unattended. Watch oil and equipment condition to prevent accidents.

rst-1-q216.objective: Serve promptly and accurately explain storage conditions and limits for takeaway.
rst-1-q216.stem: What is wrong with saying all food is safe within two hours of completion?
options: It ignores food and temperature conditions
rst-1-q216.explanation: Time alone cannot give a universal guarantee. Check food, temperature, elapsed history, and the management plan.

rst-1-q217.objective: Carry out tidying and planned cleaning, managing waste separately from food.
rst-1-q217.stem: Where should you check sorting methods for waste oil and bottles?
options: Local authority and restaurant waste rules
rst-1-q217.explanation: Separate waste by type and discard according to local requirements and restaurant procedures.

rst-1-q218.objective: Check oil and batch size to prevent uneven heating and burns.
rst-1-q218.stem: What change is likely if a stir-fry is heated for too long?
options: It becomes stew-like and loses its character
Quality stays constant even with more food
rst-1-q218.explanation: High heat and short time matter in stir-frying; prolonged heating changes texture and character.

rst-1-q219.objective: Use basic expressions appropriately and clearly confirm orders and suggestions.
rst-1-q219.stem: When should you say “お待たせいたしました” (Thank you for waiting)?
options: When bringing food the customer has waited for
To everyone met outside before entering
When putting ingredients in the refrigerator
rst-1-q219.explanation: Use it after keeping customers waiting, such as at food delivery. Choose wording suited to the situation.

rst-1-q220.objective: Classify dishes by process and control temperature and time to service for non-heated dishes.
rst-1-q220.stem: How are chilled tofu and sashimi basically classified by process?
options: Always cooled and reheated after cooking
All with the same heating process
rst-1-q220.explanation: Chilled tofu and sashimi are typical non-heated foods served cold.

rst-1-q221.objective: Explain heating methods suited to the dish and check appropriately for ingredients and equipment.
rst-1-q221.stem: Which explains direct versus indirect grilling?
options: Only whether a core thermometer can be used
Direct flame versus heat through a griddle or similar surface
rst-1-q221.explanation: Direct grilling applies flame directly; indirect grilling cooks through a griddle or frying pan.

rst-1-q222.objective: Use basic expressions appropriately and clearly confirm orders and suggestions.
rst-1-q222.stem: Which politely confirms the current order?
options: 「ご注文は以上でよろしかったでしょうか」 — “Was that all for your order?”
「ご注文は以上でよろしいでしょうか」 — “Is that all for your order?”
「注文は以上だったよね」 — “That was it, right?”
「注文はもういいですよね」 — “You are done ordering now, right?”
rst-1-q222.explanation: Use a clear, natural present-tense confirmation for the current situation, without an unnecessary past form.

rst-1-q223.objective: Classify dishes by process and control temperature and time to service for non-heated dishes.
rst-1-q223.stem: How is grilled fish served hot classified?
options: Cannot be classified by food type
rst-1-q223.explanation: Food heated and served hot belongs to group 2.

rst-1-q224.objective: Explain heating methods suited to the dish and check appropriately for ingredients and equipment.
options: Use seasoned liquid to infuse flavor
Set the surface by deep-frying in hot oil
rst-1-q224.explanation: Simmering heats in seasoned liquid, using softening and flavor absorption.

rst-1-q225.objective: Use basic expressions appropriately and clearly confirm orders and suggestions.
rst-1-q225.stem: Which expression is appropriate when receiving five thousand yen?
options: 「五千円お預かりします」 — “I have received five thousand yen.”
「五千円からお預かりします」 — “I have received from five thousand yen.”
「五千円に変わります」 — “It changes to five thousand yen.”
「五千円のほうになります」 — “It is on the five-thousand-yen side.”
rst-1-q225.explanation: State the received amount clearly without unnecessary “kara” or similar wording.

rst-1-q226.objective: Classify dishes by process and control temperature and time to service for non-heated dishes.
rst-1-q226.stem: A salad includes boiled ingredients that are cooled. What additional point should you check?
options: Skip temperatures based on appearance after cooling
Skip cooling records from service time alone
rst-1-q226.explanation: Do not classify by dish name alone; check control points in actual heating and cooling processes.

rst-1-q227.objective: Explain heating methods suited to the dish and check appropriately for ingredients and equipment.
rst-1-q227.stem: Why can steaming cook liquid ingredients inside containers?
options: It directly applies flame to food
Food must be submerged in oil
rst-1-q227.explanation: Steaming uses heat from water vapor and can heat ingredients held in containers.

rst-1-q228.objective: Use basic expressions appropriately and clearly confirm orders and suggestions.
rst-1-q228.stem: How should you confirm the restaurant abbreviation “aiko” with a customer?
options: 「アイスコーヒーでございますね」 — “An iced coffee, correct?”
「アイコ一本でいいね」 — “One aiko is fine, yeah?”
「いつもの略語で頼んでください」 — “Please order using our usual abbreviations.”
「略語が分からないなら注文できません」 — “You cannot order if you do not know the abbreviation.”
rst-1-q228.explanation: Do not impose internal abbreviations on customers. Confirm with the full product name.

rst-1-q229.objective: Classify dishes by process and control temperature and time to service for non-heated dishes.
rst-1-q229.stem: What is a main purpose of washing vegetables served without heating?
rst-1-q229.explanation: Without a final heating step, proper ingredient treatment and chilled control are important.

rst-1-q230.objective: Explain heating methods suited to the dish and check appropriately for ingredients and equipment.
rst-1-q230.stem: What should you watch for when opening a steamer lid?
options: Bring your face close before steam escapes
Ignore steam direction if wearing gloves
rst-1-q230.explanation: Steam can burn. Open according to procedure so it does not hit the face or hands.

rst-1-q231.objective: Use basic terms appropriately for the situation and clearly confirm orders and suggestions.
rst-1-q231.stem: You take a message while the manager is away. Which response is appropriate?
options: Everything is invalid because the manager is absent.
I will pass your message on to the manager.
I will delete the reservation without telling anyone.
rst-1-q231.explanation: Record the message and use polite language to pass it accurately to the responsible person.

rst-1-q232.objective: Connect cooking methods with checks at the center of food and stop serving if heating is insufficient.
rst-1-q232.stem: Why must hands and plates be clean when plating cooked food?
options: To change the type of ingredients
rst-1-q232.explanation: Food can remain unsafe if contaminated during plating after cooking. Keep hands, utensils, and dishes clean.

rst-1-q233.objective: Control hand and utensil hygiene and storage in processes without a final heating step.
rst-1-q233.stem: Why is hygiene still needed when mixing cooked potatoes into a salad?
options: Cooked food cannot become contaminated after cooling
The salad may not be reheated after mixing
rst-1-q233.explanation: Prevent contamination during final preparation even with cooked ingredients, and control storage conditions.

rst-1-q234.objective: Use basic terms appropriately for the situation and clearly confirm orders and suggestions.
rst-1-q234.stem: What should staff understand before recommending an item?
options: The product’s features and the customer’s preferences
Only the name of the most expensive item
Only how much the neighboring table paid
rst-1-q234.explanation: Accurate product knowledge and recommendations suited to customers support satisfaction and sales.

rst-1-q235.objective: Connect cooking methods with checks at the center of food and stop serving if heating is insufficient.
rst-1-q235.stem: What must be checked when making hamburger steaks of a new size?
options: Whether the center reaches the required heat under those conditions
Only the previous amount of meat
rst-1-q235.explanation: Changing the size can change cooking requirements. Check that the process heats the food sufficiently.

rst-1-q236.objective: Control hand and utensil hygiene and storage in processes without a final heating step.
rst-1-q236.stem: Which glove practice is appropriate when shaping rice balls?
options: Use the same gloves for taking payment and shaping rice balls
Skip all handwashing when wearing gloves
Use gloves placed on a wet floor
Use task-appropriate gloves with clean hands
rst-1-q236.explanation: Gloves do not replace handwashing. Change them as needed after touching dirty objects.

rst-1-q237.objective: Listen carefully, repeat details for confirmation, and pass on messages politely when the other person’s facial expressions are not visible.
rst-1-q237.stem: What should you say before putting a caller on hold?
options: That an unconfirmed reservation has been finalized
That you will connect them to the responsible person and ask them to wait briefly
rst-1-q237.explanation: Politely explain why the caller needs to wait and what you will do, then pass on the request accurately.

rst-1-q238.objective: Understand the risks of leaving food after cooking and link cooling, storage, and reheating records.
rst-1-q238.stem: When cooling food in a large container, what check is especially important?
options: The color of the container label
Whether the center of the food has cooled
rst-1-q238.explanation: Refrigeration alone does not guarantee the center has cooled. Check actual temperature and time according to the restaurant’s procedure.

rst-1-q239.objective: Control hand and utensil hygiene and storage in processes without a final heating step.
rst-1-q239.stem: What effect can occur when a dressed dish releases water?
options: Storage temperature no longer needs checking
Ingredient labeling is no longer needed
The taste or vinegar concentration changes
rst-1-q239.explanation: Water changes the taste and vinegar concentration, affecting quality and control. Pay attention to batch size and storage conditions.

rst-1-q240.objective: Listen carefully, repeat details for confirmation, and pass on messages politely when the other person’s facial expressions are not visible.
rst-1-q240.stem: What should you say first when answering after the phone has rung three or more times?
options: All dishes are sold out today
rst-1-q240.explanation: The textbook’s telephone example adds an acknowledgment of the wait at the start when the phone has rung three or more times.

rst-1-q241.objective: Understand the risks of leaving food after cooking and link cooling, storage, and reheating records.
rst-1-q241.stem: What should take priority when selecting a cooling method?
options: Avoid prolonged time in the temperature danger zone
Wait at room temperature until food looks cool
Combine food in a deep layer in a large pot
rst-1-q241.explanation: Cool promptly after cooking and control temperature and time. Check the method in the restaurant’s plan.

rst-1-q242.objective: Match equipment names to their functions and distinguish heating, hot holding, cooling, and storage.
rst-1-q242.stem: Which cooking methods are mainly suited to a griddle?
options: Grilling on a flat plate and stir-frying
rst-1-q242.explanation: A griddle uses a flat surface such as an iron plate, mainly for grilling and stir-frying.

rst-1-q243.objective: Listen carefully, repeat details for confirmation, and pass on messages politely when the other person’s facial expressions are not visible.
rst-1-q243.stem: What must be passed on after taking a telephone message?
options: Discard the record if the request is difficult
Give the responsible person the request and the caller’s contact details
rst-1-q243.explanation: For a request you cannot answer, confirm and record its details and the contact information, then reliably pass it to the responsible person.

rst-1-q244.objective: Understand the risks of leaving food after cooking and link cooling, storage, and reheating records.
rst-1-q244.stem: Why divide food being cooled into shallow containers?
options: To let heat escape more easily
To make its shelf life unlimited
rst-1-q244.explanation: Adjust quantity and depth to allow rapid cooling. Hygiene and actual temperature checks are still necessary.

rst-1-q245.objective: Match equipment names to their functions and distinguish heating, hot holding, cooling, and storage.
rst-1-q245.stem: Which specialized equipment cooks noodles in hot water?
rst-1-q245.explanation: A noodle boiler cooks noodles by boiling; it has a different purpose from cooling and packaging equipment.

rst-1-q246.objective: Listen carefully, repeat details for confirmation, and pass on messages politely when the other person’s facial expressions are not visible.
rst-1-q246.stem: Which basic way of ending a call matches the textbook?
options: Check that the other person has hung up, then hang up quietly
Hang up first while the conversation is unfinished
Walk away silently with the call on hold
rst-1-q246.explanation: The example shows finishing the caller’s request and hanging up quietly after the other person ends the call.

rst-1-q247.objective: Record what was checked, when and how, and actions taken when an abnormality was found.
rst-1-q247.stem: What does “when” in a hygiene management plan define?
options: The time or occasion for checking
rst-1-q247.explanation: Specifying when checks occur makes it easier to perform them at the necessary points.

rst-1-q248.objective: Match equipment names to their functions and distinguish heating, hot holding, cooling, and storage.
rst-1-q248.stem: How do a rice warmer and a rice cooker differ in purpose?
options: One keeps cooked rice warm; the other cooks rice
rst-1-q248.explanation: A rice cooker cooks rice, while a rice warmer keeps already cooked rice warm.

rst-1-q249.objective: Check ingredients and preparation processes and refer to the responsible person without giving unverified safety assurances.
rst-1-q249.stem: Why must seasonings also be checked for food allergy information?
options: All seasonings have the same ingredients
rst-1-q249.explanation: Sauces and processed ingredients may contain allergens. Check the latest ingredient information.

rst-1-q250.objective: Record what was checked, when and how, and actions taken when an abnormality was found.
rst-1-q250.stem: What belongs under “when a problem occurs” in a hygiene plan?
options: Actions such as returning unacceptable deliveries
rst-1-q250.explanation: Decide in advance how to handle abnormalities so that action can be taken when they are discovered.

rst-1-q251.objective: Match equipment names to their functions and distinguish heating, hot holding, cooling, and storage.
rst-1-q251.stem: Which equipment is introduced as a conveyor oven?
rst-1-q251.explanation: The jet oven is introduced as a conveyor-type oven.

rst-1-q252.objective: Check ingredients and preparation processes and refer to the responsible person without giving unverified safety assurances.
rst-1-q252.stem: What is necessary when passing an allergy-related order to the kitchen?
options: Clearly share ingredients to avoid and confirmed conditions
Treat it like an ordinary order and omit the details verbally
Assume the dish name alone is enough
rst-1-q252.explanation: Reliably share the necessary information between ordering, cooking, and serving to prevent communication omissions.

rst-1-q253.objective: Record what was checked, when and how, and actions taken when an abnormality was found.
rst-1-q253.stem: What is a benefit of keeping hygiene management records?
options: Records allow the work to be skipped
Actual temperatures are no longer needed
Implementation and areas for improvement can be reviewed later
Food expiry dates can be extended
rst-1-q253.explanation: Records help verify implementation, review problems, and improve practices, but do not replace actual hygiene work.

rst-1-q254.objective: Match equipment names to their functions and distinguish heating, hot holding, cooling, and storage.
rst-1-q254.stem: Which equipment combines a worktop with refrigerated storage?
rst-1-q254.explanation: A counter refrigerator combines a work surface with refrigeration and is also used for food storage.

rst-1-q255.objective: Check ingredients and preparation processes and refer to the responsible person without giving unverified safety assurances.
rst-1-q255.stem: Why does removing visible egg not guarantee an allergy-safe dish?
options: Only visible egg counts as an allergenic ingredient
Components may remain in other ingredients or through contact
Moving to another plate removes all transferred components
rst-1-q255.explanation: Other ingredients and contact must also be checked. Removing visible egg alone cannot provide a guarantee.

rst-1-q256.objective: Record what was checked, when and how, and actions taken when an abnormality was found.
rst-1-q256.stem: Why must you not enter someone else’s name as the checker in a record?
options: It prevents tracing who performed the check
rst-1-q256.explanation: Keep records based on the actual checker and facts so that events can be reviewed later.

rst-1-q257.objective: Match equipment names to their functions and distinguish heating, hot holding, cooling, and storage.
rst-1-q257.stem: What role does a blast chiller serve when choosing cooling equipment?
rst-1-q257.explanation: A blast chiller rapidly cools food; distinguish its role from a refrigerator used simply for storage.

rst-1-q258.objective: Check ingredients and preparation processes and refer to the responsible person without giving unverified safety assurances.
rst-1-q258.stem: What warning follows from breathing difficulties being possible as well as a rash?
options: All symptoms resolve if you wait
Diluting the dish with water always solves the problem
rst-1-q258.explanation: Severe reactions can be life-threatening, making information checks and prompt emergency action important.

rst-1-q259.objective: Record what was checked, when and how, and actions taken when an abnormality was found.
rst-1-q259.stem: A record of abnormal temperature only states that it was remeasured. What else should be recorded?
options: When the abnormality was found and what action was taken
Only the person’s name, omitting the action
rst-1-q259.explanation: Recording actual abnormal readings, time, affected items, reports, and actions supports later decisions.

rst-1-q260.objective: Relate dishwashing and ingredient-processing equipment to its purpose and safe operation.
rst-1-q260.stem: Which purpose fits a conveyor-type dishwasher?
options: Filleting a fish into three pieces
Automatically washing large quantities of dishes and similar items
rst-1-q260.explanation: A conveyor-type dishwasher is large equipment used to automatically wash many dishes and utensils.

rst-1-q261.objective: Distinguish fermented and distilled alcoholic drinks and perform necessary age and driving checks.
rst-1-q261.stem: Which category do wine and sake share?
rst-1-q261.explanation: Wine and sake are fermented alcoholic drinks produced using yeast fermentation.

rst-1-q262.objective: Classify food safety hazards and stop use and report when an abnormality is found.
rst-1-q262.stem: Why are glass fragments and detergent treated as different hazards?
options: Physical foreign objects and chemicals require different controls
rst-1-q262.explanation: Hard foreign objects and chemicals enter food through different routes and need different controls, so distinguish them for prevention.

rst-1-q263.objective: Relate dishwashing and ingredient-processing equipment to its purpose and safe operation.
rst-1-q263.stem: Why remove dirt before putting utensils in a sterilizing cabinet?
options: The cabinet does not replace washing
rst-1-q263.explanation: Disinfection may be insufficient when dirt remains. Wash properly first.

rst-1-q264.objective: Distinguish fermented and distilled alcoholic drinks and perform necessary age and driving checks.
rst-1-q264.stem: Which category do brandy and whisky share?
rst-1-q264.explanation: Brandy and whisky are examples of drinks distilled after fermentation.

rst-1-q265.objective: Apply the three principles for preventing bacterial food poisoning throughout the work process.
options: Leave finished dishes at room temperature for a long time
Separate utensils for raw meat and vegetables eaten raw
Take all refrigerated food out at once
rst-1-q265.explanation: Separate utensils prevent bacteria from ingredients being transferred to other food.

rst-1-q266.objective: Relate dishwashing and ingredient-processing equipment to its purpose and safe operation.
rst-1-q266.stem: What is the main use of a cutter mixer?
rst-1-q266.explanation: A cutter mixer is introduced as equipment for chopping and mixing ingredients.

rst-1-q267.objective: Distinguish fermented and distilled alcoholic drinks and perform necessary age and driving checks.
rst-1-q267.stem: Which main beer ingredient matches the textbook?
rst-1-q267.explanation: The textbook lists barley and similar grains as the main ingredients of beer. Also check each product’s label.

rst-1-q268.objective: Understand sources of major bacteria and select prevention suited to the food and task.
rst-1-q268.stem: Why combine heating and separation to control bacteria on raw meat?
options: To control both contamination spread before heating and bacteria in food
To make every type of meat identical
Always store vegetables eaten raw together with meat
rst-1-q268.explanation: Heating is not enough; work practices must also prevent transferring bacteria from raw meat to other food.

rst-1-q269.objective: Relate dishwashing and ingredient-processing equipment to its purpose and safe operation.
rst-1-q269.stem: What is appropriate for food after vacuum packing?
options: Always keep it indefinitely at room temperature
Remove every label and lot code
Always serve raw meat without heating
Follow the specified temperature and use-by limit
rst-1-q269.explanation: Vacuum packing does not remove the need to manage storage temperature and expiry limits.

rst-1-q270.objective: Distinguish fermented and distilled alcoholic drinks and perform necessary age and driving checks.
rst-1-q270.stem: Which main sake ingredient matches the textbook?
rst-1-q270.explanation: The textbook identifies rice as the ingredient for Japanese sake such as seishu and nigorizake.

rst-1-q271.objective: Explain why hazards other than bacteria cannot be assessed by ordinary heating or refrigeration alone.
rst-1-q271.stem: Which example meets the freezing condition for Anisakis control?
rst-1-q271.explanation: Conditions given for Anisakis control include −20℃ for at least 24 hours. Manage the process so the actual food meets them.

rst-1-q272.objective: Check cooking utensil names and purposes to prevent misuse and contamination.
rst-1-q272.stem: Which deep cylindrical pot is used for large quantities of soup and similar liquids?
rst-1-q272.explanation: A stockpot is a deep pot used for soup and similar dishes. Check the capacity that can be handled safely.

rst-1-q273.objective: Distinguish fermented and distilled alcoholic drinks and perform necessary age and driving checks.
rst-1-q273.stem: When serving alcohol to someone planning to operate a vehicle, how should bicycles be treated?
options: No check is needed unless it is a car
Serve alcohol to everyone in a group
rst-1-q273.explanation: When serving alcohol, check for people who will ride bicycles and similar vehicles as well as drive cars.

rst-1-q274.objective: Explain why hazards other than bacteria cannot be assessed by ordinary heating or refrigeration alone.
rst-1-q274.stem: Which combination is given for heating against Anisakis?
options: 70℃ or above, or 60℃ for at least 1 minute
Only washing in cold water or soaking in salt water
Only browning the surface or curing in vinegar
rst-1-q274.explanation: Ensure the food meets the stated parasite-control conditions and also perform visual checks and preparation measures.

rst-1-q275.objective: Check cooking utensil names and purposes to prevent misuse and contamination.
rst-1-q275.stem: Which knife is introduced for cutting vegetables?
rst-1-q275.explanation: The nakiri is introduced as a vegetable knife. Separate tools by purpose and handle them hygienically.

rst-1-q276.objective: Distinguish fermented and distilled alcoholic drinks and perform necessary age and driving checks.
rst-1-q276.stem: What should you note if a customer only says “I am an adult” during an age check?
options: Always serve alcohol to any adult
Asking a companion always removes the need to verify the customer
Verify that the customer is at least 20 using the required method
Ordering food removes the need for age checks
rst-1-q276.explanation: The drinking age is 20. Do not rely only on a claim of adulthood; follow the restaurant’s verification procedure.

rst-1-q277.objective: Check both order details and hygiene condition to identify unacceptable items.
rst-1-q277.stem: Why must expiry labels be checked against the actual items even for the same product?
options: Checking the name erases the expiry date
Reading a label means the food has been heated
Matching the order and quantity alone cannot establish quality
rst-1-q277.explanation: At receiving, check expiry dates, packaging, and storage conditions as well as product names and quantities.

rst-1-q278.objective: Check cooking utensil names and purposes to prevent misuse and contamination.
rst-1-q278.stem: What combination should be checked when selecting a hotel pan?
options: Only depth, without checking heat resistance
Do not distinguish cooling and heating use if sizes match
Do not check food suitability if the lid fits
Purpose, size, and suitability for the food
rst-1-q278.explanation: Check that container material and shape suit storage or cooking, the food, and the temperature.

rst-1-q279.objective: Distinguish fermented and distilled alcoholic drinks and perform necessary age and driving checks.
rst-1-q279.stem: What role does a “handle keeper” have in a group?
options: Not drinking alcohol and driving the car
rst-1-q279.explanation: A handle keeper is the designated driver who does not drink alcohol. Do not serve that person alcohol.

rst-1-q280.objective: Check refrigerator temperature, storage limits, and abnormality responses as a connected process.
rst-1-q280.stem: Why does repairing a refrigerator after a temperature fault not mean all the food is usable?
options: Refrigerator temperature is unrelated to food
The duration of the fault and food condition also affect safety
Correcting the setting makes shelf life unlimited
rst-1-q280.explanation: Equipment recovery and food safety verification are separate. Report the history and condition to the responsible person for a decision.

rst-1-q281.objective: Check cooking utensil names and purposes to prevent misuse and contamination.
rst-1-q281.stem: Which utensil is suitable for cutting bread?
rst-1-q281.explanation: Use the knife introduced for bread according to the restaurant’s assigned purposes.

rst-1-q282.objective: Use the main functions of nutrients and taste differences in basic explanations of dishes.
rst-1-q282.stem: What main function do fats and carbohydrates share?
rst-1-q282.explanation: Fats and carbohydrates provide energy and should be consumed in balance with protein and other nutrients.

rst-1-q283.objective: Break contamination routes from raw ingredients to prepared food.
rst-1-q283.stem: What is the problem with packing prepared vegetables and raw meat in the same container?
options: Bacteria from raw meat may transfer to the vegetables
It always makes the container lighter
rst-1-q283.explanation: Control ingredient separation and contact routes, especially to prevent contamination of food that will not be heated.

rst-1-q284.objective: Check cooking utensil names and purposes to prevent misuse and contamination.
rst-1-q284.stem: Which utensil is suitable for boiling and lifting noodles?
rst-1-q284.explanation: A tebo is introduced as a mesh utensil used when boiling noodles.

rst-1-q285.objective: Use the main functions of nutrients and taste differences in basic explanations of dishes.
rst-1-q285.stem: What is added to the three macronutrient groups to make the five nutrient groups?
rst-1-q285.explanation: The five nutrient groups consist of the three main groups plus vitamins and minerals.

rst-1-q286.objective: Classify food safety hazards and stop use and report when an abnormality is found.
rst-1-q286.stem: In food poisoning classifications, which category includes hepatitis E virus?
rst-1-q286.explanation: The textbook classifies hepatitis E virus as a cause of viral food poisoning, distinguishing it from bacteria.

rst-1-q287.objective: Check cooking utensil names and purposes to prevent misuse and contamination.
rst-1-q287.stem: What utensil feature should be checked when serving equal portions of soup?
options: The capacity of the ladle or similar utensil
rst-1-q287.explanation: For consistent portions, check utensil capacity and the restaurant’s standard serving size.

rst-1-q288.objective: Use the main functions of nutrients and taste differences in basic explanations of dishes.
rst-1-q288.stem: What basic taste joins sweet, salty, sour, and bitter?
rst-1-q288.explanation: Umami is also a basic taste and belongs to a different category from temperature and hardness.

rst-1-q289.objective: Remove dirt before proper disinfection and prevent chemical mix-ups.
rst-1-q289.stem: What is the problem with skipping rinsing and proceeding to disinfection?
options: Detergent and similar residues may remain
rst-1-q289.explanation: Rinse away detergent and dirt thoroughly before proceeding to the specified disinfection.

rst-1-q290.objective: Measure weight, core temperature, surface temperature, and time using appropriate instruments.
rst-1-q290.stem: Why use refrigerator thermometers and probe thermometers differently?
options: Only the appearance of the numbers differs
They measure different targets: cabinet air and food interiors
Both are only for weighing food
rst-1-q290.explanation: Choose instruments suited to the target and measurement position and check values appropriate to the purpose.

rst-1-q291.objective: Use the main functions of nutrients and taste differences in basic explanations of dishes.
rst-1-q291.stem: Which pairing of basic taste and example is correct?
rst-1-q291.explanation: Lemon and vinegar exemplify sourness, unlike sugar’s sweetness and salt’s saltiness.

rst-1-q292.objective: Relate meat fat and connective tissue characteristics to cutting and cooking method choices.
rst-1-q292.stem: Which nutrient is particularly mentioned for pork tenderloin and leg?
rst-1-q292.explanation: Pork tenderloin is described as rich in vitamin B1, with leg also high, second to tenderloin.

rst-1-q293.objective: Measure weight, core temperature, surface temperature, and time using appropriate instruments.
rst-1-q293.stem: What does zeroing the scale before weighing food relate to?
rst-1-q293.explanation: Weight including the container does not show the net ingredient amount, so subtract the container weight.

rst-1-q294.objective: Use the main functions of nutrients and taste differences in basic explanations of dishes.
rst-1-q294.stem: Which explanation of taste perception is appropriate?
options: It is always identical for everyone
Its intensity varies by person and health condition
It depends only on the number of dishes
rst-1-q294.explanation: Taste varies by individual and health condition, so confirm preferences and provide polite guidance.

rst-1-q295.objective: Check personal health and appearance and report food-related abnormalities without hiding them.
rst-1-q295.stem: Why check protection when handling food with a bandaged finger?
options: To remove the need for heating
To manage the wound and the risk of the bandage entering food
rst-1-q295.explanation: Report and protect the wound and follow the restaurant’s glove and other procedures. Handwashing is still necessary.

rst-1-q296.objective: Measure weight, core temperature, surface temperature, and time using appropriate instruments.
rst-1-q296.stem: Which purpose pairing is correct for a kitchen timer and hygrometer?
options: Checking oil color and food names
rst-1-q296.explanation: A timer measures time; a hygrometer measures humidity.

rst-1-q297.objective: Use the main functions of nutrients and taste differences in basic explanations of dishes.
rst-1-q297.stem: Which main mineral function matches the textbook?
options: Building bones and teeth and regulating body functions
rst-1-q297.explanation: Distinguish the roles of the five nutrient groups and connect mineral functions with food examples.

rst-1-q298.objective: Check personal health and appearance and report food-related abnormalities without hiding them.
rst-1-q298.stem: What is wrong with covering dirty work clothes with an apron instead of changing?
options: It does not ensure clean clothing
rst-1-q298.explanation: Check the hygiene of all clothing and change dirty work clothes according to restaurant procedure.

rst-1-q299.objective: Anticipate lifting and carrying risks and choose to split loads or seek assistance.
rst-1-q299.stem: What is the risk of carrying a pot filled to the brim with hot soup?
options: Only being unable to use a cart
rst-1-q299.explanation: Avoid filling liquids to the brim. Use a stable quantity and carrying method to prevent spills and burns.

rst-1-q300.objective: Respect religious and dietary differences and specifically confirm foods the customer cannot eat.
rst-1-q300.stem: Which description of veganism matches the textbook?
options: Avoiding animal foods, including eggs and dairy
rst-1-q300.explanation: Vegan diets avoid animal foods including eggs and dairy. Confirm individual requirements too.

rst-1-q301.objective: Wash hands when changing tasks and clean thoroughly, including fingertips and thumbs.
rst-1-q301.stem: You touch a dirty tap immediately after washing your hands. What should you consider before the next task?
options: Whether the hands have become contaminated again
Contact is irrelevant because hands were washed
rst-1-q301.explanation: Prevent recontamination after handwashing and clean hands again if necessary.

rst-1-q302.objective: Anticipate lifting and carrying risks and choose to split loads or seek assistance.
rst-1-q302.stem: Which posture is suitable for lifting heavy loads?
options: Stand away and lift suddenly using only the lower back
Lift while twisting the body sharply
Move close, use the legs, and lift slowly
rst-1-q302.explanation: Hold steadily, align the back, and use the legs. Split excessive loads or ask for help.

rst-1-q303.objective: Respect religious and dietary differences and specifically confirm foods the customer cannot eat.
rst-1-q303.stem: What is the basic meaning of halal?
rst-1-q303.explanation: Halal means permitted. Check requirements including seasonings and processes.

rst-1-q304.objective: Tidy and clean according to a plan and manage waste separately from food.
rst-1-q304.stem: Drains were omitted from the cleaning plan. Which improvement is appropriate?
options: Add the locations and frequency and perform the work
Exclude them if surfaces look clean
Skip all records on busy days
Leave them until responsibility sorts itself out
rst-1-q304.explanation: Make the cleaning plan specific and sustain it, including areas that are not usually visible.

rst-1-q305.objective: Anticipate lifting and carrying risks and choose to split loads or seek assistance.
rst-1-q305.stem: What is the risk of stacking loads too high on a cart?
options: Movement can topple the load and obstruct forward vision
rst-1-q305.explanation: High stacks are unstable and obstruct vision. Keep quantities and placement stable.

rst-1-q306.objective: Respect religious and dietary differences and specifically confirm foods the customer cannot eat.
rst-1-q306.stem: Why check the stock before recommending a vegetable dish to a vegetarian?
options: It may contain meat- or fish-derived ingredients
Dish color alone reveals the requirements
rst-1-q306.explanation: Check stock and seasonings as well as visible ingredients and compare them with the customer’s exclusions.

rst-1-q307.objective: Tidy and clean according to a plan and manage waste separately from food.
rst-1-q307.stem: What container does the textbook specify for waste from pufferfish preparation?
options: Store it in a lockable container
Mix it indiscriminately with ordinary food waste
Leave it open on a food refrigerator shelf
Wash it all down the sink
rst-1-q307.explanation: The textbook gives a lockable container as an example for pufferfish waste. In practice, check restaurant rules and local handling requirements.

rst-1-q308.objective: Anticipate lifting and carrying risks and choose to split loads or seek assistance.
rst-1-q308.stem: Which is a benefit of a dry kitchen?
options: Helping prevent falls and unhygienic conditions
rst-1-q308.explanation: Keeping floors dry helps prevent slipping and creates a hygienic environment.

rst-1-q309.objective: Respect religious and dietary differences and specifically confirm foods the customer cannot eat.
rst-1-q309.stem: Which response should be avoided for a customer with religious or dietary requirements?
options: Deciding what they can eat solely from nationality
Asking them which ingredients to avoid
Explaining what the restaurant can accommodate
Checking seasonings with the responsible person
rst-1-q309.explanation: Dietary requirements vary individually. Do not assume from appearance or nationality; ask the customer.

rst-1-q310.objective: Classify dishes by process and control temperature and time until service for unheated dishes.
rst-1-q310.stem: Why combine temperature and time at HACCP control points?
options: Time is always irrelevant if temperature is known
Food type is unnecessary if time is known
The cooking method name decides everything
Duration under conditions favoring bacterial growth also matters
rst-1-q310.explanation: Time spent in the temperature danger zone also affects safety, so control both according to the process.

rst-1-q311.objective: Distinguish safety procedures during use and cleaning and handle blades safely.
rst-1-q311.stem: Ingredients need pushing while a machine blade is rotating. What is appropriate?
options: Push directly by hand if wearing gloves
Push with a finger at low speed
Check the specified safe method and do not put a hand inside
Remove the blade with power on
rst-1-q311.explanation: Never put hands into rotating equipment. Follow machine-specific safety procedures, including stopping it.

rst-1-q312.objective: Perform checks in order before and after service and hand over unfinished tasks.
rst-1-q312.stem: Why check change and slips before opening?
options: To prepare for smooth payment handling
rst-1-q312.explanation: Preparing the till and recording forms is necessary for payments when service begins.

rst-1-q313.objective: Classify dishes by process and control temperature and time until service for unheated dishes.
rst-1-q313.stem: What does cold storage of unheated food mainly suppress?
options: The size of all foreign objects
rst-1-q313.explanation: Bacteria may remain after washing. Control low temperatures and time to suppress growth.

rst-1-q314.objective: Distinguish safety procedures during use and cleaning and handle blades safely.
rst-1-q314.stem: When cleaning a slicer, what safety action should be checked after switching it off?
options: Put a hand inside while the blade moves
Unplug it and verify a complete stop
rst-1-q314.explanation: Follow procedures for stopping, power isolation, and complete blade stoppage before cleaning.

rst-1-q315.objective: Perform checks in order before and after service and hand over unfinished tasks.
rst-1-q315.stem: What matters when cleaning seating areas during closing work?
options: Deep-clean beside guests as soon as closing time arrives
Avoid spoiling remaining guests’ meals or impressions
rst-1-q315.explanation: Even after closing time, adjust work order and location with consideration for remaining guests.

rst-1-q316.objective: Connect cooking methods with checks at the center of food and stop serving if heating is insufficient.
rst-1-q316.stem: Which core heating condition is given for bacterial control in meat?
rst-1-q316.explanation: The meat bacterial-control example is a core temperature of 75℃ for at least 1 minute. Check restaurant conditions for the food and hazard.

rst-1-q317.objective: Distinguish safety procedures during use and cleaning and handle blades safely.
rst-1-q317.stem: Which storage practice is appropriate after using a knife?
options: Submerge it in a full sink
Wash it and put it in its designated place
rst-1-q317.explanation: Do not leave blades hidden. Wash them and return them to the assigned storage place.

rst-1-q318.objective: Perform checks in order before and after service and hand over unfinished tasks.
rst-1-q318.stem: A scheduled employee is absent before opening. What is appropriate for assigning roles?
options: Assign nobody and rely on everyone noticing
Postpone safety checks without assigning anyone
Keep the old roster without reporting the shortage
Review staffing with the responsible person and clarify assignments
rst-1-q318.explanation: Opening preparation includes checking staff and roles. Report shortages and reassign responsibilities.

rst-1-q319.objective: Connect cooking methods with checks at the center of food and stop serving if heating is insufficient.
rst-1-q319.stem: What management is still needed after a core temperature reading meets the standard?
options: Contamination and temperature control during plating and until service
rst-1-q319.explanation: After heating, prevent secondary contamination and hazards from unsuitable temperatures or times.

rst-1-q320.objective: Distinguish safety procedures during use and cleaning and handle blades safely.
rst-1-q320.stem: Why call out when moving with a knife?
options: To alert others to the blade
rst-1-q320.explanation: Alert others to the knife’s presence to prevent contact accidents.

rst-1-q321.objective: Choose cleaning tools and order suited to the area and check what customers can see.
rst-1-q321.stem: What is the basic order for cleaning high shelves and floors?
options: Start high and finish with the floor
Finish the floor before dusting shelves
Use one cloth everywhere without an order
rst-1-q321.explanation: Dust falls downward, so work from high areas to low areas.

rst-1-q322.objective: Isolate chipped items or fragments when found and handle chemicals correctly.
rst-1-q322.stem: Why distinguish ceramic and glass items when washing?
options: Material strength differs and breakage can occur
rst-1-q322.explanation: Handle items according to material strength to avoid collisions causing cracks or chips.

rst-1-q323.objective: Understand the risks of leaving food after cooking and link cooling, storage, and reheating records.
rst-1-q323.stem: Food is still warm after the planned cooling time. What information is needed?
options: Start time, measured temperature, and method used
rst-1-q323.explanation: Report cooling history and methods specifically and obtain instructions on usability and other decisions.

rst-1-q324.objective: Choose cleaning tools and order suited to the area and check what customers can see.
rst-1-q324.stem: What is the problem with immediately wiping dry dust with a wet cloth?
options: It may make dirt harder to remove
All periodic cleaning can be skipped
rst-1-q324.explanation: Remove dry dirt by a method suited to its condition and clean in the appropriate order.

rst-1-q325.objective: Isolate chipped items or fragments when found and handle chemicals correctly.
rst-1-q325.stem: What problem is likely when dishes are stacked too high?
rst-1-q325.explanation: Excessive stacks can fall or break. Handle stable quantities.

rst-1-q326.objective: Understand the risks of leaving food after cooking and link cooling, storage, and reheating records.
rst-1-q326.stem: What matters when using FDA cooling examples and Japanese catering-facility cooling examples?
options: Combine whichever temperatures and times are convenient
Call both laws for every restaurant
Let each employee choose conditions outside the plan
Check applicability and sources and do not mix figures
rst-1-q326.explanation: The textbook includes reference examples with different scopes. Follow the verified plan adopted by the restaurant.

rst-1-q327.objective: Choose cleaning tools and order suited to the area and check what customers can see.
rst-1-q327.stem: What is the main purpose of soaking?
options: Loosening stuck-on dirt for easier removal
rst-1-q327.explanation: Soaking is a pretreatment to loosen dirt, not a replacement for necessary washing and disinfection.

rst-1-q328.objective: Isolate chipped items or fragments when found and handle chemicals correctly.
rst-1-q328.stem: A small crack is found on a dish rim. What is appropriate?
options: Use it if the inside is clean
Use it only for hot food
Remove it from use and separate it
Turn it away from the customer
rst-1-q328.explanation: Do not use cracked or chipped dishes because they can cause injuries or foreign-object contamination.

rst-1-q329.objective: Record what was checked, when and how, and actions taken when an abnormality was found.
rst-1-q329.stem: Why read the hygiene plan’s response to abnormal refrigerator temperature?
options: To pretend a temperature was measured
To understand what action to take immediately
rst-1-q329.explanation: The plan specifies abnormality responses to implement when an actual problem is found.

rst-1-q330.objective: Choose cleaning tools and order suited to the area and check what customers can see.
rst-1-q330.stem: Which benefit of planned air-conditioner filter cleaning is appropriate?
options: Helping prevent odors and maintain comfortable temperatures
rst-1-q330.explanation: Clean air-conditioning equipment helps maintain comfort and a clean environment.

rst-1-q331.objective: Isolate chipped items or fragments when found and handle chemicals correctly.
rst-1-q331.stem: Why should alcohol spray not be used near flames?
rst-1-q331.explanation: Alcohol is flammable. Do not spray it near flames.

rst-1-q332.objective: Record what was checked, when and how, and actions taken when an abnormality was found.
rst-1-q332.stem: What is wrong with marking every record “good” before doing the work?
options: Only that recording times are identical
The entries are not actual check results
rst-1-q332.explanation: Record actual check results; never prefill them as good.

rst-1-q333.objective: Choose cleaning tools and order suited to the area and check what customers can see.
rst-1-q333.stem: You find fraying in the seating-area carpet. What is needed besides cleaning?
options: Report the condition and arrange repair
Ignore it because it is not dirt
Have customers step on it to fix it
rst-1-q333.explanation: Equipment deterioration affects comfort and safety. Report it and arrange maintenance when noticed.

rst-1-q334.objective: Isolate chipped items or fragments when found and handle chemicals correctly.
rst-1-q334.stem: Why display dilution instructions for detergents and disinfectants?
options: So everyone can prepare the correct concentration
To remove the need to read labels
rst-1-q334.explanation: Clear instructions based on product requirements prevent concentration errors.

rst-1-q335.objective: Classify food safety hazards and stop use and report when an abnormality is found.
rst-1-q335.stem: Why is heating alone insufficient when metal fragments may be in food?
options: Ordinary heating cannot remove hard foreign objects
rst-1-q335.explanation: Physical foreign objects differ from microbial hazards and require contamination prevention and isolation of affected items.

rst-1-q336.objective: Match amounts and payment methods to prevent duplicate charges and change errors.
rst-1-q336.stem: Which Japanese banknote denomination is listed in the textbook?
rst-1-q336.explanation: The 2,000-yen note is a Japanese banknote. Follow the restaurant’s checking procedure if unfamiliar with it.

rst-1-q337.objective: Inspect fire sources and electrical equipment and choose safe actions without attempting unsafe firefighting.
rst-1-q337.stem: How should you hold a plug when unplugging it?
options: Hold the plug body, not the cord
Pull hard on the middle of the cord
Grip metal parts with wet hands
Pour water on the socket while unplugging
rst-1-q337.explanation: Hold the plug to avoid damaging the cord and do not touch it with wet hands.

rst-1-q338.objective: Apply the three principles for preventing bacterial food poisoning throughout the work process.
rst-1-q338.stem: Why are heating and other controls still needed after thawing frozen food?
options: Freezing does not kill every bacterium
Packaging removes the need for handwashing
rst-1-q338.explanation: Freezing suppresses growth but is not disinfection. Continue food-appropriate controls after thawing.

rst-1-q339.objective: Match amounts and payment methods to prevent duplicate charges and change errors.
rst-1-q339.stem: Which set of Japanese coin denominations is correct?
rst-1-q339.explanation: The textbook lists coins of 1, 5, 10, 50, 100, and 500 yen.

rst-1-q340.objective: Inspect fire sources and electrical equipment and choose safe actions without attempting unsafe firefighting.
rst-1-q340.stem: Why pay attention to dust between sockets and plugs?
options: To store refrigerated food at room temperature
rst-1-q340.explanation: Dust around electrical equipment and cord damage are also part of daily fire-prevention checks.

rst-1-q341.objective: Classify food safety hazards and stop use and report when an abnormality is found.
rst-1-q341.stem: Which food-poisoning cause category do Anisakis and roundworms share?
rst-1-q341.explanation: The textbook gives Anisakis and roundworms as examples of parasitic causes of food poisoning.

rst-1-q342.objective: Match amounts and payment methods to prevent duplicate charges and change errors.
rst-1-q342.stem: Which debit-card payment feature is appropriate?
options: The amount is deducted from the account immediately
Charges are always combined the following year
They only work with paper meal tickets
rst-1-q342.explanation: The textbook describes debit cards as deducting the amount from the account when used.

rst-1-q343.objective: Inspect fire sources and electrical equipment and choose safe actions without attempting unsafe firefighting.
rst-1-q343.stem: Where should flammable spray cans not be stored?
options: A designated place meeting product conditions
A hot place in direct sun or near flames
A safe place separate from food
rst-1-q343.explanation: Store flammable spray cans appropriately away from high temperatures and flames.

rst-1-q344.objective: Explain why hazards other than bacteria cannot be assessed by ordinary heating or refrigeration alone.
rst-1-q344.stem: Why does visual parasite inspection alone not complete all controls?
options: Food-appropriate treatment and control conditions must also be checked
Visually inspected fish are all sterile
Raw internal organs may then be served
rst-1-q344.explanation: Combine visual checks, gut removal, and necessary freezing or heating with measures suited to the food.

rst-1-q345.objective: Match amounts and payment methods to prevent duplicate charges and change errors.
rst-1-q345.stem: Which credit-card feature matches the textbook?
options: Always deducting the entire balance immediately
rst-1-q345.explanation: The textbook classifies credit cards as deferred payment. Check which brands the restaurant accepts.

rst-1-q346.objective: Inspect fire sources and electrical equipment and choose safe actions without attempting unsafe firefighting.
rst-1-q346.stem: Why keep waste frying-oil containers away from fire sources?
options: To always return oil to edible use
rst-1-q346.explanation: Manage waste oil in covered containers and do not place them near flames.

rst-1-q347.objective: Identify fish parts as instructed and explain seasonality including regional differences.
rst-1-q347.stem: What is the part covering a fish’s gills called?
rst-1-q347.explanation: The fish diagram identifies the gill cover as covering the gills, distinct from fins and the lateral line.

rst-1-q348.objective: Match amounts and payment methods to prevent duplicate charges and change errors.
rst-1-q348.stem: Which payment method is introduced as a top-up type?
rst-1-q348.explanation: The textbook gives electronic money as a top-up example. Check the actual method against the restaurant’s contract and product.

rst-1-q349.objective: Inspect fire sources and electrical equipment and choose safe actions without attempting unsafe firefighting.
rst-1-q349.stem: Which basic extinguisher operation order is correct?
options: Squeeze lever → reinsert pin → turn away
Pull pin → aim nozzle at fire source → squeeze lever
Aim at a person → pull pin → throw it
Open the body → remove contents by hand
rst-1-q349.explanation: The textbook’s order is pin, nozzle, lever. Prioritize evacuation over unsafe firefighting.

rst-1-q350.objective: Check refrigerator temperature, storage limits, and abnormality responses as a connected process.
rst-1-q350.stem: What should be checked when choosing refrigerator items to use first during expiry checks?
options: Only whether an item is at the front
Each food’s label and usable time limit
rst-1-q350.explanation: Check expiry limits along with cold storage and use food within its limit.

rst-1-q351.objective: Match amounts and payment methods to prevent duplicate charges and change errors.
rst-1-q351.stem: When a customer scans the restaurant’s code to pay, what is necessary?
options: Treat everything as complete without checking the screen
Check the amount and payment result by restaurant procedure
rst-1-q351.explanation: Check the amount and payment result using the restaurant’s method, not just that the code was scanned.

rst-1-q352.objective: Relate meat fat and connective tissue characteristics to cutting and cooking method choices.
rst-1-q352.stem: Which feature of beef inside round matches the textbook?
rst-1-q352.explanation: The textbook identifies inside round as a low-fat beef cut.

rst-1-q353.objective: Break contamination routes from raw ingredients to prepared food.
rst-1-q353.stem: Raw-meat packaging has meat juice outside. Which route beyond the food needs attention?
rst-1-q353.explanation: Dirt outside containers can transfer through hands and equipment to other food.

rst-1-q354.objective: Match amounts and payment methods to prevent duplicate charges and change errors.
rst-1-q354.stem: Why check which cashless methods the restaurant accepts?
options: The same terminal accepts all methods regardless of contract
Accepting cards means accepting all electronic money
A customer app removes the need to check restaurant support
Support differs by contract and terminal
rst-1-q354.explanation: Know the latest accepted methods because availability depends on the restaurant’s contract and equipment.

rst-1-q355.objective: Relate meat fat and connective tissue characteristics to cutting and cooking method choices.
rst-1-q355.stem: Which way of preparing beef outside round for stir-frying matches the textbook?
options: Warm a large block only briefly
Add connective tissue and serve raw
Slice thinly or cut into small pieces
rst-1-q355.explanation: Outside round is a somewhat firm lean cut; examples include thin slicing or small pieces for stir-frying.

rst-1-q356.objective: Check cooking utensil names and purposes to prevent misuse and contamination.
rst-1-q356.stem: Which colander materials are introduced in the textbook?
rst-1-q356.explanation: Examples include stainless-steel and plastic colanders. Use one suited to purpose and temperature.

rst-1-q357.objective: Listen to customers, preserve items and facts, and report accurately to the responsible person.
rst-1-q357.stem: What should you say when a complaint exceeds your authority?
options: Explain that you will call the responsible person and report promptly
Leave for a long time without explanation
rst-1-q357.explanation: When a decision is difficult, explain to the customer and refer to the responsible person.

rst-1-q358.objective: Relate meat fat and connective tissue characteristics to cutting and cooking method choices.
rst-1-q358.stem: What description do beef katabara and tomobara share?
options: All are always as tender as tenderloin
rst-1-q358.explanation: Both have layered lean and fat. Also check firmness and suitability for dishes.

rst-1-q359.objective: Separate cleaning tools and worn equipment and clean contact surfaces too.
rst-1-q359.stem: What is wrong with touching a kitchen handle with gloves used for toilet cleaning?
options: Dry glove surfaces cannot transfer contamination
No change is needed without direct food contact
Later wiping the handle means gloves need not be changed immediately
rst-1-q359.explanation: Pay attention to equipment-removal order and touched surfaces to avoid carrying contamination out of the cleaning area.

rst-1-q360.objective: Listen to customers, preserve items and facts, and report accurately to the responsible person.
rst-1-q360.stem: Why mainly preserve a dish containing a foreign object?
options: To give it to another guest
To remove the object and serve it again
To examine the item and investigate cause and impact
rst-1-q360.explanation: Preserve the dish and object by restaurant procedure for checks by the responsible person and kitchen.

rst-1-q361.objective: Listen to customers, preserve items and facts, and report accurately to the responsible person.
rst-1-q361.stem: Whose input is needed when deciding to remake a dish containing a foreign object?
options: The customer’s wishes and the restaurant’s responsible person
rst-1-q361.explanation: Handle remakes and charges after checking customer wishes and restaurant authority and rules.

rst-1-q362.objective: Relate meat fat and connective tissue characteristics to cutting and cooking method choices.
rst-1-q362.stem: What is bone-in pork belly called?
rst-1-q362.explanation: The textbook calls bone-in pork belly spare ribs. Distinguish the animal and cut.

rst-1-q363.objective: Express welcome and apologies with clean appearance and calm movements.
rst-1-q363.stem: Which fragrance consideration is appropriate for service appearance?
options: Cover sweat only with strong perfume
Change strong perfume for each dish
Strong fragrance makes uniform dirt irrelevant
rst-1-q363.explanation: The textbook says to avoid strong perfume. Maintain cleanliness and restrained grooming suited to dining.

rst-1-q364.objective: Listen to customers, preserve items and facts, and report accurately to the responsible person.
rst-1-q364.stem: How should a complaint identifying a bone as a foreign object be received?
options: Give it to another guest without inspection
Check it as a hazard and complaint even if it is part of an ingredient
rst-1-q364.explanation: Ingredient parts such as bones can still cause injuries and complaints. Check the circumstances and item.

rst-1-q365.objective: Relate meat fat and connective tissue characteristics to cutting and cooking method choices.
rst-1-q365.stem: Which beef rump description matches the textbook?
options: Tender lean meat with depth of flavor
The most connective tissue of every cut
rst-1-q365.explanation: Beef rump is described as tender lean meat used in many dishes, including steak.

rst-1-q366.objective: Wash hands when changing tasks and clean thoroughly, including fingertips and thumbs.
rst-1-q366.stem: What does the textbook state about washing hands twice?
options: Repeat washing with soap and rinsing
rst-1-q366.explanation: It describes repeating the steps from soap washing through running-water rinsing as effective.

rst-1-q367.objective: Listen to customers, preserve items and facts, and report accurately to the responsible person.
rst-1-q367.stem: What is appropriate when unsure whether to charge for food in a foreign-object complaint?
options: The staff member decides everyone’s bill
Discard the item and continue payment
Interrupt the customer to demand payment
rst-1-q367.explanation: Charges and compensation follow authority and rules. Consult the responsible person.

rst-1-q368.objective: Identify fish parts as instructed and explain seasonality including regional differences.
rst-1-q368.stem: Which seafood is given as an autumn example?
rst-1-q368.explanation: Autumn examples include bonito. Check actual seasonality and deliveries, including production areas.

rst-1-q369.objective: Check cooking utensil names and purposes to prevent misuse and contamination.
rst-1-q369.stem: Which utensil is listed together with “kettle”?
rst-1-q369.explanation: The utensil list gives yakan and kettle together. Match restaurant terminology to the actual item.

rst-1-q370.objective: Listen to customers, preserve items and facts, and report accurately to the responsible person.
rst-1-q370.stem: Why mainly avoid paper clips and staplers near food?
options: To prevent metal and other foreign-object contamination
rst-1-q370.explanation: Do not use them near food to prevent small metal pieces and similar objects entering it.

rst-1-q371.objective: Use major vegetable categories and approximate seasons in ingredient checks and customer guidance.
rst-1-q371.stem: Which category includes eggplant, tomato, and cucumber?
rst-1-q371.explanation: The textbook classifies them as fruit vegetables because the fruit is used.

rst-1-q372.objective: Classify dishes by process and control temperature and time until service for unheated dishes.
rst-1-q372.stem: Which range is closely related to avoiding prolonged holding in the danger zone?
rst-1-q372.explanation: The textbook describes 10–60℃ as a zone favorable to bacterial growth, controlled together with time.

rst-1-q373.objective: Listen to customers, preserve items and facts, and report accurately to the responsible person.
rst-1-q373.stem: After catching an insect in the seating area, what should still be checked?
options: Record only the number caught and stop investigating
Check only seating, not routes to the kitchen
Assume more chemicals remove the need to check entry routes
rst-1-q373.explanation: To prevent contamination, investigate and improve causes of insect breeding or entry, not just remove insects.

rst-1-q374.objective: Use major vegetable categories and approximate seasons in ingredient checks and customer guidance.
rst-1-q374.stem: Which season is given for bamboo shoots, rapeseed blossoms, and asparagus?
rst-1-q374.explanation: The textbook lists them as spring examples. Origin and climate can cause variation.

rst-1-q375.objective: Connect cooking methods with checks at the center of food and stop serving if heating is insufficient.
rst-1-q375.stem: Why does oil at 180℃ not mean the food’s center is also 180℃?
options: Oil and food interiors are different measurement locations
All thermometers display the same value
rst-1-q375.explanation: Heating-medium and core temperatures differ. Check at the required position.

rst-1-q376.objective: Ensure safety, communicate symptoms, request emergency help when necessary, and coordinate within the restaurant.
rst-1-q376.stem: A guest has altered consciousness and swallowing ability is uncertain. What should be avoided?
rst-1-q376.explanation: Do not force food or drink when consciousness or swallowing is impaired. Follow emergency instructions.

rst-1-q377.objective: Prepare the required quantity and prevent temperature rises and contamination during preparation.
rst-1-q377.stem: Which preparation example adds seasoning in advance?
rst-1-q377.explanation: Preparation includes quantity calculations, washing, cutting, and preseasoning such as marinating.

rst-1-q378.objective: Understand the risks of leaving food after cooking and link cooling, storage, and reheating records.
rst-1-q378.stem: What facts should be recorded when cooling equipment is used?
options: A mark deciding in advance there is no abnormality
rst-1-q378.explanation: Equipment use alone does not prove conditions were met. Check actual time and temperature according to the plan.

rst-1-q379.objective: Ensure safety, communicate symptoms, request emergency help when necessary, and coordinate within the restaurant.
rst-1-q379.stem: What information should be ready to give first when calling emergency services?
options: Today’s sales and spending per guest
Restaurant location and the guest’s condition
rst-1-q379.explanation: Give location, symptoms, consciousness, and breathing details so responders can arrive and understand the situation.

rst-1-q380.objective: Connect cutting names with finished shapes and explain why uniform sizes matter.
rst-1-q380.stem: What shape feature results from cutting ingredients diagonally?
rst-1-q380.explanation: Diagonal cutting of long ingredients increases the cut surface area.

rst-1-q381.objective: Record what was checked, when and how, and actions taken when an abnormality was found.
rst-1-q381.stem: Why separate important-control records by dish process?
rst-1-q381.explanation: Unheated, heated, cooled, and reheated processes have different controls. Use process-appropriate records.

rst-1-q382.objective: Ensure safety, communicate symptoms, request emergency help when necessary, and coordinate within the restaurant.
rst-1-q382.stem: What comes before investigating the cause of a suspected severe allergic reaction?
options: Calling for assistance and necessary emergency help
rst-1-q382.explanation: In urgent situations, prioritize safety and emergency response and pass known information to medical personnel.

rst-1-q383.objective: Connect cutting names with finished shapes and explain why uniform sizes matter.
options: A half-round cut in half again
rst-1-q383.explanation: The textbook describes shiraga as extremely fine julienne, distinct from other shapes and sizes.

rst-1-q384.objective: Classify food safety hazards and stop use and report when an abnormality is found.
